title.zh: 卷一百五十七 列傳第一百〇七: 王翃 郗士美 李鄘 辛秘 馬摠 韋弘景 王彥威
title.en: Volume 157 Biographies 107: Wang Hong, Chi Shimei, Li Yong, Xinmi, Ma Hui, Wei Hongjing, Wang Yanwei

sentences.zh: 李光進，本河曲部落稽阿跌之族也。

translations.literal: Li Guangjin—Li Guangjin was originally of the Jie A Die clan among the Hequ tribal groups.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangjin was a member of the Jie A Die people, one of the tribal confederations of the Hequ region.

sentences.zh: 父良臣，襲雞田州刺史，隸朔方軍。

translations.literal: His father Liangchen inherited the post of prefect of Jitian Prefecture and was attached to the Shuofang army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liangchen had inherited the prefecture of Jitian and served under the Shuofang army.

sentences.zh: 光進姊適舍利葛旃，殺僕固瑒而事河東節度使辛雲京。

translations.literal: Guangjin's elder sister married Sheli Gezhan, who killed Pugu Chang and entered the service of Hedong military commissioner Xin Yunjing.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin's elder sister was married to Sheli Gezhan, who killed Pugu Chang and then served Hedong military commissioner Xin Yunjing.

sentences.zh: 光進兄弟少依葛旃，因家於太原。

translations.literal: The Guangjin brothers in youth relied on Gezhan and thus made their home in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In their youth the Guangjin brothers had depended on Gezhan, and they settled their household in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 光進勇毅果敢，其武藝兵略次於葛旃。

translations.literal: Guangjin was brave, resolute, and decisive; in martial skill and military strategy he was second only to Gezhan.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin was bold, steadfast, and resolute, and in arms and strategy he ranked only below Gezhan.

sentences.zh: 肅宗自靈武觀兵，光進從郭子儀破賊，收兩京，累有戰功。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong reviewed the troops at Lingwu, Guangjin followed Guo Ziyi in defeating the rebels, recovering the two capitals, and repeatedly achieved merit in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong mustered his forces at Lingwu, Guangjin followed Guo Ziyi in breaking the rebels, retaking the two capitals, and winning repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 至德中，授代州刺史，封范陽郡公，食邑二百戶。

translations.literal: In the Zhide era he was appointed prefect of Daizhou, enfeoffed as Duke of Fanyang, with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhide period he was made prefect of Daizhou and created Duke of Fanyang with an income of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 上元初，郭子儀為朔方節度，以軍討大同、橫野、清夷，范陽及河北殘寇，用光進為都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shangyuan era Guo Ziyi was military commissioner of Shuofang; campaigning with the army against the remnant bandits at Datong, Hengye, Qingyi, Fanyang, and Hebei, he employed Guangjin as overall commander of army and cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shangyuan reign Guo Ziyi, as Shuofang military commissioner, led campaigns against remnant rebels in Datong, Hengye, Qingyi, Fanyang, and Hebei, and appointed Guangjin overall commander of troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 尋遷渭北節度使。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to be military commissioner of Weibei.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to military commissioner of Weibei.

sentences.zh: 永泰初，進封武威郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongtai era he was advanced in rank to Prince of Wuwei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yongtai period he was promoted to Prince of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 大歷四年，檢校戶部尚書，知省事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dali he was made acting Minister of Revenue and directed routine business at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Dali era he was appointed acting Minister of Revenue with charge of Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又轉檢校刑部尚書、兼太子太保。

translations.literal: Before long he was again transferred to acting Minister of Justice and concurrently Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he was reassigned as acting Minister of Justice and concurrent Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 是歲冬十月，葬母於京城之南原，將相致祭者凡四十四幄，窮極奢靡，城內士庶，觀者如堵。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter that year he buried his mother on the southern plateau outside the capital; generals and ministers who came to offer sacrifice set up forty-four pavilions in the utmost extravagance, and within the city commoners and gentry watched in crowds thick as a wall.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, he buried his mother on the southern heights outside the capital. Forty-four pavilions were erected for the rites of generals and ministers, with lavish display beyond measure, and the city's people packed the streets to watch.

sentences.zh: 元和四年，王承宗反。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhe Wang Chengzong rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanhe, Wang Chengzong rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 范希朝引師救易定，表光進為步都虞候，戰於木刀溝，光進有功。

translations.literal: Fan Xichao led troops to relieve Yiding and memorialized Guangjin as infantry chief adjutant; fighting at Mudao Gully, Guangjin achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xichao marched to relieve Yiding and recommended Guangjin as chief infantry adjutant. At the battle of Mudao Gully Guangjin distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 六年，拜銀青光祿大夫、檢校工部尚書，充單於大都護、振武節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Silver Gleam Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Minister of Works, and served as Grand Protector of Chanyu and military commissioner of Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he received the title Silver Gleam Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and acting Minister of Works, and was made Grand Protector of Chanyu and military commissioner of Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 詔以光進夙有誠節，克著茂勛，賜姓李氏。

translations.literal: An edict stated that because Guangjin had long shown loyal integrity and clearly achieved splendid merit, the surname Li was bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that Guangjin, having long proved his loyalty and won outstanding merit, was granted the imperial surname Li.

sentences.zh: 其弟光顏除洺州刺史，充本州團練使。

translations.literal: His younger brother Guangyan was appointed prefect of Mingzhou and served as regimental training commissioner of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Guangyan was made prefect of Mingzhou and regimental training commissioner of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 兄弟恩澤同時，人皆嘆異。

translations.literal: The brothers received imperial favor at the same time, and all marveled at the circumstance.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers received imperial favor together, and people everywhere remarked on the rarity of it.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷靈武節度使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to military commissioner of Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to military commissioner of Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 光進嘗從馬燧救臨洺，戰洹水，收河中，皆有功。

translations.literal: Guangjin had followed Ma Sui in relieving Linming, fought at the Huan River, and recovered Hezhong—at each he achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin had followed Ma Sui in the relief of Linming, fought at the Huan River, and helped recover Hezhong, earning credit in each campaign.

sentences.zh: 前後軍中之職，無所不歷；

translations.literal: Before and after he had held every post in the army;
translations.idiomatic: Over the years he had held every kind of army post;

sentences.zh: 中丞、大夫悉曾兼帶。

translations.literal: and had at various times concurrently held the ranks of censor and grand master.
translations.idiomatic: and had at one time or another concurrently borne the titles of censor and grand master.

sentences.zh: 先是救易定之師，光進、光顏皆在其行，故軍中呼光進為大大夫，光顏為小大夫。

translations.literal: Earlier, on the expedition to relieve Yiding, both Guangjin and Guangyan had been in the column, so the army called Guangjin the Elder Grand Master and Guangyan the Younger Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: When the army had marched to relieve Yiding, both Guangjin and Guangyan had been in the ranks, so the troops called Guangjin the Elder Grand Master and Guangyan the Younger Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 十年七月卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the tenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month of the tenth year.

sentences.zh: 光進兄弟少以孝睦推於軍中。

translations.literal: The Guangjin brothers in youth were esteemed in the army for filial piety and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: From youth the Guangjin brothers were known in the army for their filial devotion and brotherly harmony.

sentences.zh: 及居母喪，三年不歸寢室。

translations.literal: When they were in mourning for their mother, for three years they did not return to the marital chamber.
translations.idiomatic: During their mother's mourning they abstained from the marital bed for the full three years.

sentences.zh: 光顏先娶妻，其母委以家事。

translations.literal: Guangyan had married first, and their mother entrusted him with household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan had married first, and their mother had put him in charge of the household.

sentences.zh: 母卒，光進始娶。

translations.literal: When the mother died, Guangjin married for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: Only after their mother's death did Guangjin take a wife.

sentences.zh: 光顏使其妻奉管籥、家籍、財物，歸於其姒。

translations.literal: Guangyan had his wife present the keys, household registers, and property to return them to his elder brother's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan had his wife hand over the keys, household records, and goods to their sister-in-law.

sentences.zh: 光進命反之，且謂光顏曰：「新婦逮事母，嘗命以主家，不可改也。」

translations.literal: Guangjin ordered them returned and said to Guangyan, "The new wife served our mother and was once commanded to manage the household—this must not be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin ordered everything returned and told Guangyan, "Your wife served our mother and was charged to run the house—that must not be altered."

sentences.zh: 因相持泣良久，乃如初。

translations.literal: Thereupon they embraced each other and wept for a long time, and matters returned to how they had been.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers then held each other and wept for a long while before everything was restored as before.

sentences.zh: 卒時年六十五，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: At death he was sixty-five years old and was posthumously awarded Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-five at his death and was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 光顏與兄光進以葛旃善騎射，兄弟自幼皆師之，葛旃獨許光顏之勇健，己不能逮。

translations.literal: Guangyan and his elder brother Guangjin, because Gezhan excelled at mounted archery, from childhood both brothers studied under him; Gezhan alone acknowledged Guangyan's valor and vigor as beyond his own reach.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan and his brother Guangjin had studied horsemanship and archery under Gezhan from boyhood. Gezhan alone declared that Guangyan's courage and strength surpassed what he himself could match.

sentences.zh: 及長，從河東軍為裨將，討李懷光、楊惠琳，皆有功。

translations.literal: When grown he served with the Hedong army as a deputy commander; campaigning against Li Huai'guang and Yang Huilin, he achieved merit in each.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he served in the Hedong army as a deputy commander and won distinction in campaigns against Li Huai'guang and Yang Huilin.

sentences.zh: 後隨高崇文平蜀，搴旗斬將，出入如神，由是稍稍知名。

translations.literal: Later he followed Gao Chongwen in pacifying Shu, seizing enemy banners and slaying generals, entering and leaving the fray like a spirit; from this he gradually became known.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Gao Chongwen in the pacification of Shu, tearing down banners and cutting down enemy officers with seemingly supernatural speed, and from that time his name slowly spread.

sentences.zh: 自憲宗元和已來，歷授代、洺二州刺史、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: From the Yuanhe era of Emperor Xianzong onward he successively received appointment as prefect of Dai and Ming prefectures, concurrently Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Xianzong's Yuanhe reign onward he served in turn as prefect of Dai and Ming and as concurrent Grand Censor.

sentences.zh: 九年，將討淮、蔡，九月，遷陳州刺史，充忠武軍都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, as a campaign against Huai and Cai was planned, in the ninth month he was transferred to prefect of Chenzhou and appointed overall commander of troops and horses of the Zhongwu army.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, with a campaign against Huai and Cai in preparation, he was transferred in the ninth month to prefect of Chenzhou and overall commander of the Zhongwu army's troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 逾月，遷忠武軍節度使、檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was transferred to military commissioner of the Zhongwu army and acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later he became military commissioner of the Zhongwu army and acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷征天下兵，環申、蔡而討吳元濟，詔光顏以本軍獨當一面。

translations.literal: Just then the court mobilized troops from throughout the realm, encircling Shen and Cai to campaign against Wu Yuanji, and ordered Guangyan to hold one front alone with his own army.
translations.idiomatic: The court then raised armies from across the empire to surround Shen and Cai and attack Wu Yuanji, charging Guangyan to hold an entire sector with his own forces.

sentences.zh: 光顏於是引兵臨溵水，抗洄曲。

translations.literal: Guangyan thereupon led his troops to the Yin River and confronted Huaiqu.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan marched his army to the Yin River and took position opposite Huaiqu.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，破元濟之師於時曲。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the following year he defeated Yuanji's army at Shiqu.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the fifth month, he routed Yuanji's forces at Shiqu.

sentences.zh: 初，賊眾晨壓光顏之壘而陣，光顏不得出，乃自毀其柵之左右，出騎以突之。

translations.literal: At first the rebel masses at dawn pressed Guangyan's ramparts and formed battle lines; Guangyan could not get out, so he himself tore down sections of his palisade to left and right and led cavalry out in a charge.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the rebels had pressed against Guangyan's camp and drawn up in battle order, pinning him inside. He tore gaps in his own palisade to either side and led his cavalry out in a charge.

sentences.zh: 光顏將數騎冒堅而沖之，出入者數四。

translations.literal: Guangyan led several horsemen through the enemy's solid ranks in repeated charges, going in and out four times.
translations.idiomatic: Leading a handful of horsemen, Guangyan plunged through the enemy line again and again, riding in and out four times.

sentences.zh: 賊眾盡識，矢集於身如蝟。

translations.literal: The rebel masses all recognized him, and arrows clustered on his body like spines on a hedgehog.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels all knew him on sight, and arrows bristled on his body like quills on a hedgehog.

sentences.zh: 其子攬光顏馬鞅，止其深入。

translations.literal: His son seized Guangyan's saddle flap to stop him from pressing deeper.
translations.idiomatic: His son caught hold of Guangyan's saddle flap to keep him from riding farther in.

sentences.zh: 光顏舉刃叱之，乃退。

translations.literal: Guangyan raised his blade and shouted at him, and only then did he withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan raised his blade and shouted him down before he would fall back.

sentences.zh: 於是人爭奮躍。

translations.literal: Thereupon the men all strove to leap forward in ardor.
translations.idiomatic: At that the men surged forward with renewed fury.

sentences.zh: 賊乃大潰，死者數千人。

translations.literal: The rebels then broke in great rout, and several thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke and fled in disorder, leaving several thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 捷聲至京師，人人相賀。

translations.literal: News of victory reached the capital, and everyone congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: Word of the victory reached the capital, and people everywhere rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 時伐蔡之師，大小凡十余鎮，自裴度使還，唯奏光顏勇而知義，終不辱命。

translations.literal: At that time the forces campaigning against Cai, large and small, numbered more than ten commands; since Pei Du's return from his mission he had memorialized only that Guangyan was brave and understood righteousness and would never disgrace his commission.
translations.idiomatic: More than a dozen commands, great and small, were then campaigning against Cai. After Pei Du returned from his inspection tour, he reported to the throne that Guangyan alone was both brave and principled and would never fail his charge.

sentences.zh: 至是，果立功焉。

translations.literal: By this time he had indeed achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Now, as predicted, he had won a decisive victory.

sentences.zh: 是歲十一月，光顏又與懷汝節度烏重胤同破元濟之眾於小溵河，平其柵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year Guangyan again, together with Huairu military commissioner Wu Chongyin, defeated Yuanji's forces at the Xiao Shen River and leveled their palisades.
translations.idiomatic: That November Guangyan joined Huairu military commissioner Wu Chongyin in defeating Yuanji's troops at the Xiao Shen River and leveling their stockades.

sentences.zh: 初，都統韓弘令諸軍齊攻賊城，賊又徑攻烏重胤之壘。

translations.literal: Earlier supreme commander Han Hong had ordered all armies to attack the rebel city together, but the rebels in turn struck directly at Wu Chongyin's ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme commander Han Hong had ordered a joint assault on the rebel city, but the rebels turned and attacked Wu Chongyin's camp head-on.

sentences.zh: 重胤禦之，中數槍，馳請救於光顏。

translations.literal: Chongyin withstood them, was struck by several spears, and galloped to Guangyan to beg for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyin held them off but took several spear wounds and rode in haste to ask Guangyan for help.

sentences.zh: 光顏以小溵橋賊之堡也，乘其無備，使田穎、宋朝隱襲而取之。

translations.literal: Guangyan, because the rebels' fort at Xiao Shen Bridge was their strongpoint, took advantage of their unpreparedness and sent Tian Ying and Song Chaoyin to raid and seize it.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan saw that the rebel fort at Xiao Shen Bridge was their key position. While they were off guard he sent Tian Ying and Song Chaoyin to storm and take it.

sentences.zh: 乃平其城塹，由是克救重胤。

translations.literal: He then leveled their walls and moats, and thereby was able to rescue Chongyin.
translations.idiomatic: He leveled their walls and ditches and so was able to relieve Chongyin.

sentences.zh: 韓弘以光顏違令，取穎及朝隱將戮之。

translations.literal: Han Hong, because Guangyan had disobeyed orders, took Tian Ying and Chaoyin and was about to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hong, holding that Guangyan had defied his orders, seized Tian Ying and Chaoyin and prepared to put them to death.

sentences.zh: 穎及朝隱勇而材，軍中皆惋惜之。

translations.literal: Ying and Chaoyin were brave and talented, and throughout the army all regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Ying and Chaoyin were brave and able men, and the whole army mourned the prospect of their execution.

sentences.zh: 光顏畏弘不敢留。

translations.literal: Guangyan feared Hong and dared not keep them.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan, fearing Han Hong, did not dare to keep them.

sentences.zh: 會中使景忠信至，知其情，乃矯詔令所在械系之。

translations.literal: It happened that palace envoy Jing Zhongxin arrived, learned the situation, and forged an edict ordering that wherever they were they be put in fetters and escorted.
translations.idiomatic: Palace envoy Jing Zhongxin arrived, learned what was happening, and forged an edict ordering the men seized and bound wherever found.

sentences.zh: 走馬入見，具以本末聞。

translations.literal: He galloped in to an audience and reported the whole sequence of events.
translations.idiomatic: He rode posthaste to court and reported the full story to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 憲宗赦忠信矯詔罪，令即往釋穎及朝隱。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong pardoned Zhongxin's crime of forging an edict and ordered him to go at once and release Ying and Chaoyin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong pardoned Zhongxin for forging the edict and ordered him to go immediately and free Ying and Chaoyin.

sentences.zh: 弘及光顏叠以表論。

translations.literal: Hong and Guangyan submitted memorial upon memorial arguing the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hong and Guangyan sent repeated memorials debating the case.

sentences.zh: 憲宗謂弘使曰：「穎等違都統令，固當處死。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong said to Hong's envoy, "Ying and the others disobeyed the supreme commander's orders and should indeed be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong told Han Hong's envoy, "Ying and the others defied the supreme commander's orders and deserve death.

sentences.zh: 但光顏以其襲賊有功，亦可宥之。

translations.literal: Yet because Guangyan's raid on the rebels achieved merit, they may also be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: But Guangyan's raid on the enemy was meritorious, so they may be spared as well.

sentences.zh: 軍有三令五申，宜舍此以收來效。」

translations.literal: The army has its repeated commands and admonitions; it is fitting to set this aside to secure future service."
translations.idiomatic: An army lives by repeated orders and warnings. Let this go and win their future service instead."

sentences.zh: 及以詔諭弘，弘不悅。

translations.literal: When the edict was conveyed to Hong, he was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict reached Han Hong, he was displeased.

sentences.zh: 十一年，光顏連敗元濟之眾，拔賊淩雲柵，憲宗大悅，賜其告捷者奴婢銀錦。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Guangyan repeatedly defeated Yuanji's forces, captured the rebels' Lingyun palisade, and Emperor Xianzong was greatly pleased and bestowed on the bearer of the victory report slave women, silver, and brocade.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Guangyan defeated Yuanji's forces again and again and took the rebel Lingyun stockade. Emperor Xianzong was delighted and rewarded the messenger of victory with slave women, silver, and brocade.

sentences.zh: 進位檢校尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan was promoted to acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 十二年四月，光顏敗元濟之眾三萬於郾城。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twelfth year Guangyan defeated thirty thousand of Yuanji's forces at Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twelfth year Guangyan routed thirty thousand of Yuanji's troops at Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 其將張伯良奔於蔡州，殺其賊什二三，獲馬千匹，器甲三萬聯，皆畫雷公符。

translations.literal: His general Zhang Boliang fled to Caizhou; they killed two or three tenths of the rebels, captured a thousand horses and thirty thousand sets of armor and weapons, all painted with the Thunder Lord talisman.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji's general Zhang Boliang fled to Caizhou. Guangyan's men killed two or three tenths of the enemy force, took a thousand horses and thirty thousand sets of arms and armor, each marked with the Thunder Lord talisman.

sentences.zh: 仍書云：「速破城北軍。」

translations.literal: They also bore inscriptions saying, "Quickly break the northern army outside the city."
translations.idiomatic: They also bore inscriptions reading, "Break the northern army outside the city at once."

sentences.zh: 尋而郾城守將鄧懷金請以城降。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Yancheng's defending general Deng Huaijin asked to surrender the city.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yancheng's defender Deng Huaijin offered to surrender the city.

sentences.zh: 光顏許之，而收郾城。

translations.literal: Guangyan agreed and took possession of Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan accepted, and Yancheng fell into his hands.

sentences.zh: 初，鄧懷金以官軍圍青陵城，絕其歸路，懷金懼，謀於郾城令董昌齡。

translations.literal: Earlier Deng Huaijin, because the government army had besieged Qingling and cut off his line of retreat, was afraid and consulted with Yancheng magistrate Dong Changling.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the imperial army had besieged Qingling and cut off his retreat, Huaijin grew afraid and took counsel with Yancheng magistrate Dong Changling.

sentences.zh: 昌齡母素誡其子令降，昌齡因此勸懷金歸款於光顏，且曰：「城中之人，父母妻子皆質於蔡州，如不屈而降，則家盡屠矣。

translations.literal: Changling's mother had long admonished her son to surrender; Changling therefore urged Huaijin to submit to Guangyan, saying, "The people in the city—all their parents, wives, and children are held hostage in Caizhou; if you do not pretend to resist and then surrender, their families will all be slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Changling's mother had long urged her son to surrender. He therefore persuaded Huaijin to submit to Guangyan, saying, "Everyone in the city has parents, wives, and children held hostage in Caizhou. Unless you feign resistance and then surrender, their families will be slaughtered to the last person.

sentences.zh: 請來攻城，我則舉烽求救。

translations.literal: Please come attack the city; I will raise beacon fires to call for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Ask Guangyan to attack the city. I will light beacon fires to summon rebel reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 救兵將至，官軍逆擊之必敗，此時當以城降。」

translations.literal: When the rescue troops arrive, if the government army meets them head-on it will surely be defeated; at that moment you should surrender the city."
translations.idiomatic: When the relief force arrives, the imperial army can strike them head-on and rout them. That is the moment to surrender the city."

sentences.zh: 光顏從之，賊果敗走。

translations.literal: Guangyan followed this plan, and the rebels were indeed defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan agreed. The rebels were routed and fled as planned.

sentences.zh: 於是昌齡執印，帥吏列於門外，懷金與諸將素服倒戈列於門內；

translations.literal: Thereupon Changling held the seal while commanders and clerks lined up outside the gate; Huaijin and the generals, in plain white dress with weapons reversed, lined up inside the gate;
translations.idiomatic: Changling then came out holding the official seal, with commanders and clerks lined up outside the gate, while Huaijin and his officers, dressed in white with weapons reversed, waited inside;

sentences.zh: 光顏受降，乃入羅城，其城自壞五十余步。

translations.literal: Guangyan accepted the surrender and then entered the outer city; fifty-odd paces of the wall had collapsed on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan accepted their surrender and entered the outer city, where more than fifty paces of wall had collapsed of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 時韓弘為汴帥，驕矜倔強。

translations.literal: At that time Han Hong was military governor of Bian and was arrogant, proud, and obstinate.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hong was then military governor of Bianzhou—proud, overbearing, and stubborn.

sentences.zh: 常倚賊勢索朝廷姑息，惡光顏力戰，陰圖撓屈，計無所施。

translations.literal: He often relied on the rebels' strength to demand indulgence from the court, hated Guangyan's hard fighting, and secretly plotted to thwart and break him, but could find no means.
translations.idiomatic: He had long used the rebels' strength to extract concessions from the court and resented Guangyan's aggressive fighting. He plotted secretly to undermine him but could find no opening.

sentences.zh: 遂舉大梁城求得一美婦人，教以歌舞弦管六博之藝，飾之以珠翠金玉衣服之具，計費數百萬，命使者送遺光顏，冀一見悅惑而怠於軍政也。

translations.literal: He then searched the great city of Daliang until he found a beautiful woman, taught her the arts of song and dance, stringed instruments, and dice games, adorned her with pearls, kingfisher feathers, gold, jade, and garments, at a cost reckoned in the millions, and ordered an envoy to send her as a gift to Guangyan, hoping that on one sight he would be delighted and enervated and slacken in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He found a beautiful woman in the great city of Daliang, trained her in song, dance, music, and games of chance, and dressed her in pearls, jade, gold, and fine silks at a cost of millions. He sent her to Guangyan through an envoy, hoping one look would beguile him and dull his zeal for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 使者即賫書先造光顏壘曰：「本使令公德公私愛，憂公暴露，欲進一妓，以慰公征役之思，謹以候命。」

translations.literal: The envoy at once carried a letter and first came to Guangyan's camp, saying, "Our commissioner, cherishing you in public and private, concerned that you endure exposure in the field, wishes to present a courtesan to comfort your thoughts amid the campaign, and respectfully awaits your command."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy arrived first at Guangyan's camp with a letter: "Our commissioner, who holds you in high regard both publicly and privately, is concerned for your hardships in the field and wishes to send a courtesan to ease the burdens of campaign. He awaits your word."

sentences.zh: 光顏曰：「今日已暮，明旦納焉。」

translations.literal: Guangyan said, "Today is already late; tomorrow morning I shall receive her."
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan replied, "It is late today. Bring her tomorrow morning."

sentences.zh: 詰朝，光顏乃大宴軍士；

translations.literal: At dawn the next day Guangyan gave a great feast for the troops;
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day he held a great feast for the army;

sentences.zh: 三軍咸集，命使者進妓。

translations.literal: the whole army assembled, and he ordered the envoy to present the courtesan.
translations.idiomatic: the whole army gathered, and he had the envoy present the courtesan.

sentences.zh: 妓至，則容止端麗，殆非人間所有，一座皆驚。

translations.literal: When the courtesan arrived, her bearing and appearance were refined and lovely, scarcely of this mortal world, and the whole assembly was startled.
translations.idiomatic: When she appeared, her grace and beauty seemed scarcely of this world, and the entire hall was struck with wonder.

sentences.zh: 光顏乃於座上謂來使曰：「令公憐光顏離家室久，舍美妓見贈，誠有以荷德也。

translations.literal: Guangyan then said from his seat to the envoy, "The commissioner pities Guangyan for being long away from wife and home and has sent this beautiful courtesan as a gift—I am truly obliged for such kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan then addressed the envoy from his seat: "The commissioner, pitying me for my long absence from home, has sent this beautiful woman as a gift. I am deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 然光顏受國家恩深，誓不與逆賊同生日月下。

translations.literal: Yet Guangyan has received the state's deep grace and has sworn not to share sun and moon with the rebel traitors.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I owe the state a profound debt and have sworn never to live under the same sky as the rebels.

sentences.zh: 今戰卒數萬，皆背妻子，蹈白刃，光顏奈何以女色為樂？」

translations.literal: Now tens of thousands of fighting soldiers have left wives and children behind and tread on naked blades—how could Guangyan take pleasure in women's beauty?"
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of my soldiers have left their wives and children behind and face naked blades. How could I indulge in pleasure while they suffer?"

sentences.zh: 言訖，涕泣嗚咽。

translations.literal: When he had finished speaking he wept and sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: As he spoke he broke into tears and sobs.

sentences.zh: 堂下兵士數萬，皆感激流涕。

translations.literal: Below the hall tens of thousands of soldiers were all moved to tears of gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Below the hall tens of thousands of soldiers wept with moved gratitude.

sentences.zh: 乃厚以縑帛酬其來使，俾領其妓自席上而回，謂使者曰：「為光顏多謝令公。

translations.literal: He then richly rewarded the envoy with silk and had him lead the courtesan back from the seat, saying to the envoy, "Convey Guangyan's deep thanks to the commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded the envoy generously with silk, had him take the courtesan back from the hall, and said, "Give the commissioner my deepest thanks.

sentences.zh: 光顏事君許國之心，死無貳矣！」

translations.literal: Guangyan's heart in serving the ruler and pledging himself to the state knows no second loyalty unto death!"
translations.idiomatic: My loyalty to the throne and the realm will never waver, even unto death!"

sentences.zh: 自此兵眾之心，彌加激勵。

translations.literal: From this the hearts of the troops were all the more stirred to ardor.
translations.idiomatic: From that day the army's spirit burned all the brighter.

sentences.zh: 及裴度至行營，率賓從於方城沱口觀板築、五溝。

translations.literal: When Pei Du arrived at the forward camp he led his retinue to Fangcheng Tuokou to inspect the stockade building and the Five Ditches.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du reached the forward camp he took his staff to Fangcheng Tuokou to inspect the fortifications and the Five Ditches.

sentences.zh: 賊遽至，註弩挺刃，勢將及度。

translations.literal: Rebels suddenly arrived, strung crossbows and brandished blades, and their momentum was about to reach Du.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels suddenly appeared, crossbows drawn and blades ready, and were about to reach Pei Du himself.

sentences.zh: 光顏決戰於前以卻之。

translations.literal: Guangyan fought a decisive battle in the van to drive them back.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan met them head-on in a pitched battle and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 時光顏預慮其來，先使田布以二百騎伏於溝中，出賊不意交擊之，度方獲免。

translations.literal: At the time Guangyan had foreseen their coming and first sent Tian Bu with two hundred horsemen to lie in ambush in a ditch; striking the rebels from an unexpected direction, Du was thereby spared.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan had anticipated the attack and sent Tian Bu ahead with two hundred cavalry concealed in a ditch. The surprise cross-assault saved Pei Du from capture.

sentences.zh: 布又先扼其溝中歸路，賊多棄騎越溝，相牽墜壓而死者千余人。

translations.literal: Bu also first blocked their route of return through the ditch; many rebels abandoned their horses to cross the ditch, pulling one another down in falls and crushings, and more than a thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Bu had also sealed off their retreat through the ditch. Many rebels abandoned their mounts to scramble across; in the crush more than a thousand perished.

sentences.zh: 是日微光顏之救，度幾陷矣。

translations.literal: That day, but for Guangyan's rescue, Du would nearly have been trapped.
translations.idiomatic: That day Pei Du would nearly have been lost but for Guangyan's rescue.

sentences.zh: 是月，賊知光顏勇冠諸將，乃悉其眾出當光顏之師。

translations.literal: That month, knowing that Guangyan's bravery surpassed all generals, the rebels then marshaled their entire force to oppose Guangyan's army.
translations.idiomatic: That month the rebels, knowing Guangyan was the boldest of the imperial generals, mustered their full strength to face his army.

sentences.zh: 時李愬乘其無備，急引兵襲蔡州，拔之，獲元濟。

translations.literal: At that time Li Su, seizing their unpreparedness, swiftly led troops to raid Caizhou, took it, and captured Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: Li Su seized the moment while they were undefended, marched swiftly on Caizhou, captured the city, and took Wu Yuanji prisoner.

sentences.zh: 董重質棄洄曲軍，入城降愬。

translations.literal: Dong Chongzhi abandoned the Huaiqu army, entered the city, and surrendered to Su.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chongzhi abandoned his army at Huaiqu, entered the city, and surrendered to Li Su.

sentences.zh: 光顏知之，躍馬入賊營，大呼以降，賊眾萬余人，皆解甲投戈請命。

translations.literal: Guangyan learned of it, leaped on his horse into the rebel camp, and shouted for surrender; more than ten thousand rebel troops all removed their armor and cast down their weapons to plead for their lives.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangyan heard the news he spurred his horse into the rebel camp and shouted for surrender. More than ten thousand rebels laid down their arms and begged for mercy.

sentences.zh: 賊平，加檢校司空。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified he was additionally appointed acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed he was made acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 十三年春，命中官宴光顏於居第，賜芻米二十余車。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirteenth year the emperor ordered a palace eunuch to feast Guangyan at his residence and bestowed more than twenty cartloads of fodder and grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirteenth year an imperial eunuch was sent to entertain Guangyan at his home, with a gift of more than twenty wagonloads of fodder and grain.

sentences.zh: 憲宗又禦麟德殿召對，賜金帶錦彩。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong also proceeded to Linde Hall to summon him for audience and bestowed a gold belt and brocade silks.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong received him in Linde Hall and presented him with a gold belt and brocade silks.

sentences.zh: 朝廷東討李師道，授光顏義成軍節度使。

translations.literal: When the court marched east to attack Li Shidao, Guangyan was appointed military commissioner of the Yicheng army.
translations.idiomatic: As the court launched its eastern campaign against Li Shidao, Guangyan was made military commissioner of the Yicheng army.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，尋赴行營。

translations.literal: Upon reaching his post he soon proceeded to the forward camp.
translations.idiomatic: He reached his command and soon joined the campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 數旬之內，再敗賊軍於濮陽，殺戮數千人，進軍深入。

translations.literal: Within several tens of days he twice defeated rebel armies at Puyang, killing several thousand men, and advanced deep into enemy territory.
translations.idiomatic: Within weeks he routed rebel forces twice at Puyang, killing thousands, and pushed deeper into enemy country.

sentences.zh: 十四年，西蕃入寇，移授邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the Western Tibetans invaded; he was transferred and appointed military commissioner of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, with the Tibetans raiding from the west, he was reassigned as military commissioner of Binning.

sentences.zh: 時鹽州為吐蕃所毀，命李文悅為刺史，令光顏充勾當修築鹽州城使。

translations.literal: At that time Yizhou had been destroyed by the Tibetans; Li Wenyue was appointed prefect, and Guangyan was ordered to serve as commissioner for the repair and construction of Yizhou's walls.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou had been wrecked by the Tibetans. Li Wenyue was appointed prefect, and Guangyan was charged with rebuilding the city's defenses.

sentences.zh: 仍許以陳許六千人隨赴邠寧。

translations.literal: He was also permitted to take six thousand men from Chen and Xu to accompany him to Binning.
translations.idiomatic: He was allowed to bring six thousand troops from his Chen-Xu command to Binning.

sentences.zh: 是歲，吐蕃侵涇原。

translations.literal: That year the Tibetans raided Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Tibetan forces invaded Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 自田縉鎮夏州，以貪猥侵撓党項羌，乃引吐蕃入寇。

translations.literal: Ever since Tian Ji had governed Xiazhou, his greedy misconduct had harassed the Tangut Qiang, who then drew the Tibetans into invasion.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tian Ji had taken command at Xiazhou, his greed and abuse had provoked the Tangut tribes and brought the Tibetans across the border.

sentences.zh: 及蕃軍攻涇州，邊將郝玼血戰始退。

translations.literal: When the Tibetan army attacked Jingzhou, the frontier general Hao Ci fought a bloody battle before they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans besieged Jingzhou, frontier commander Hao Ci fought them to a bloody standstill before they retreated.

sentences.zh: 初，光顏聞賊攻涇州，料兵赴救，邠師喧然曰：「人給五十千而不識戰陣，彼何人也！

translations.literal: Earlier, when Guangyan heard the rebels were attacking Jingzhou he mustered troops to the rescue; the Binning soldiers clamored aloud, saying, "They are given fifty thousand cash each and know nothing of battle—who are those men!
translations.idiomatic: When Guangyan heard the rebels were attacking Jingzhou he mustered troops to the rescue. The Binning soldiers erupted in protest: "Those men get fifty thousand cash apiece and don't know a battle line from a parade ground—who are they!

sentences.zh: 常額衣資不得而前蹈白刃，此何人也！」

translations.literal: Their regular pay and clothing allowance unpaid yet they march ahead onto naked blades—what sort of men are these!"
translations.idiomatic: They haven't even received their regular pay and clothing allowance, yet they march ahead onto naked blades—what sort of men are these!"

sentences.zh: 憤聲恟々不可遏。

translations.literal: Angry voices surged in uproar that could not be checked.
translations.idiomatic: The angry clamor swelled into an uproar that could not be stilled.

sentences.zh: 光顏素得士心，曲為陳說大義，言發涕流。

translations.literal: Guangyan had long won the hearts of his troops; he tactfully expounded the larger duty, and as he spoke tears streamed down.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan had always commanded his men's loyalty. He plead the larger cause with them, weeping as he spoke.

sentences.zh: 三軍感之，亦泣下，乃欣然即路，擊賊退之。

translations.literal: The whole army was moved and wept as well; they then set out gladly on the road, struck the rebels, and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: The whole army wept with him, then marched willingly to the relief. They routed the enemy and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，就加特進，仍與一子四品正員官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong succeeded to the throne, Guangyan was additionally promoted to Tejin, and one of his sons was granted a regular fourth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, Guangyan received the honorary rank of Tejin, and one son was given a regular fourth-rank post.

sentences.zh: 尋詔赴闕，賜開化裏第，進加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to the capital, granted a residence in Kaihua Ward, and advanced to Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to court, given a mansion in Kaihua Ward, and promoted to Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 穆宗以光顏功冠諸將，故召赴闕，宴賜優給。

translations.literal: Muzong, because Guangyan's merit surpassed all generals, therefore summoned him to court with feasts and generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Because Guangyan's service outshone every other general, Muzong brought him to court and showered him with feasts and gifts.

sentences.zh: 已而帶平章復鎮，所以報勛臣也。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter he returned to his command bearing the title of Grand Councillor—thus the court repaid a meritorious minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was then sent back to the frontier as Grand Councillor—Muzong's way of honoring a proven champion.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，遷鳳翔節度使，依前檢校司空、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing he was transferred to military commissioner of Fengxiang, retaining his former ranks as acting Minister of Works and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Changqing era he became military commissioner of Fengxiang, keeping his titles as acting Minister of Works and Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 歲末，復授許州節度使。

translations.literal: At year's end he was again appointed military commissioner of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before the year was out he was reassigned as military commissioner of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以光顏昔鎮陳許，頗得士心，將討鎮、冀，故有此拜。

translations.literal: Because Guangyan had once governed Chen and Xu and had well won the troops' hearts, and because the court intended to campaign against Zhen and Ji, this appointment was made.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan had once held Chen-Xu and won deep loyalty from the ranks. With a campaign against Zhen and Ji in view, the court gave him this post.

sentences.zh: 赴鎮日，宰相百僚以故事送別於章敬寺，穆宗禦通化門臨送之，賜錦彩、銀器、良馬、玉帶等物。

translations.literal: On the day he departed for his post, chancellors and the hundred officials saw him off according to custom at Zhangjing Temple; Muzong proceeded to Tonghua Gate to send him off in person and bestowed brocade silks, silver vessels, fine horses, a jade belt, and other gifts.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he left for his command, the full court saw him off at Zhangjing Temple by custom. Muzong went in person to Tonghua Gate to farewell him, gifting brocades, silverware, fine horses, and a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 二年，討王廷湊，命光顏兼深州行營諸軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year, campaigning against Wang Tingcou, Guangyan was ordered to serve concurrently as military commissioner of all armies in the Shenzhou forward camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, for the campaign against Wang Tingcou, he was named overall commander of the Shenzhou expedition.

sentences.zh: 光顏既受命而行，懸軍討賊，艱於饋運。

translations.literal: Once Guangyan accepted the commission and set out, his army advanced deep into hostile country to attack rebels, and supply transport proved arduous.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan accepted the command and marched out, but his army was deep in enemy territory and supply lines quickly became a struggle.

sentences.zh: 朝廷又以滄、景、德、棣等州俾之兼管，以其鄰賊之郡，可便飛挽。

translations.literal: The court also put Cang, Jing, De, Di, and other prefectures under his concurrent administration, since those districts bordered the rebels and could speed emergency transport.
translations.idiomatic: The court added Cang, Jing, De, Di, and neighboring prefectures to his jurisdiction, hoping their proximity to the enemy would ease rapid resupply.

sentences.zh: 光顏以朝廷制置乖方，賊帥連結，未可朝夕平定，事若差跌，即前功悉棄，乃懇辭兼鎮。

translations.literal: Guangyan held that the court's dispositions were ill judged—the rebel chieftains were linked together and could not be settled overnight; if affairs stumbled, all prior merit would be squandered—and he earnestly declined the additional commands.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan argued the court's plan was unsound: the rebel leaders were allied and would not fall quickly, and one misstep would waste everything already won. He begged off the extra territories.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾作，表祈歸鎮。

translations.literal: Soon illness set in and he memorialized asking to return to his original command.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fell ill and petitioned to return to his own headquarters.

sentences.zh: 朝廷果討賊無功而赦廷湊。

translations.literal: The court indeed failed to subdue the rebels and pardoned Tingcou.
translations.idiomatic: As he had foreseen, the campaign failed and the court pardoned Wang Tingcou.

sentences.zh: 四年，敬宗即位，正拜司徒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Jingzong succeeded to the throne, and Guangyan was formally appointed Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Emperor Jingzong took the throne and Guangyan was formally made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 汴州李絺逐其帥叛，詔光顏率陳許之師討之。

translations.literal: At Bianzhou Li Xi drove out his commander and rebelled; Guangyan was ordered to lead the Chen-Xu army against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xi at Bianzhou ousted his superior and rebelled, Guangyan was ordered to march with the Chen-Xu forces to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 營於尉氏，俄而誅絺。

translations.literal: He encamped at Weishi, and within a short time Li Xi was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He encamped at Weishi and soon Li Xi was put to death.

sentences.zh: 遷太原尹、北京留守、河東節度使，進階開府儀同三司，仍於正衙受冊司徒兼侍中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Taiyuan, Northern Capital garrison commander, and Hedong military commissioner; advanced in rank to Kaifu Yitong Sansi; and at the main court received investiture as Grand Preceptor and concurrently Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Taiyuan, garrison commander of the Northern Capital, and Hedong military commissioner, promoted to Kaifu Yitong Sansi, and formally invested at court as Grand Preceptor and Vice Director of State.

sentences.zh: 二年九月卒，年六十六，廢朝三日，贈太尉，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: In the second year, ninth month, he died at age sixty-six; court mourning was observed for three days; he was posthumously made Grand Commandant and given the posthumous title Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of the second year at sixty-six. Court business was suspended for three days. He was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant with the title "Loyal."

sentences.zh: 烏重胤，潞州牙將也。

translations.literal: Wu Chongyin was a garrison officer of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chongyin was a garrison officer at Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 元和中，王承宗叛，王師加討。

translations.literal: During the Yuanhe era Wang Chengzong rebelled and imperial armies were sent to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era Wang Chengzong rebelled and the court dispatched armies against him.

sentences.zh: 潞帥盧從史雖出軍，而密與賊通。

translations.literal: The Lu prefecture commander Lu Congshi marched out with troops but secretly maintained contact with the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congshi, military commissioner of Lu, took the field but was secretly colluding with the enemy.

sentences.zh: 時神策行營吐突承璀與從史軍相近，承璀與重胤謀，縛從史於帳下。

translations.literal: At that time Tufa Chenghui of the Shence forward camp was encamped near Congshi's army; Chenghui and Chongyin plotted together and bound Congshi in his tent.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Chenghui of the Shence expedition was camped near Lu Congshi. He and Chongyin conspired to seize Congshi in his own tent.

sentences.zh: 是日，重胤戒嚴，潞軍無敢動者。

translations.literal: That day Chongyin declared martial law, and none in the Lu army dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: That day Chongyin declared martial law, and the Lu troops did not dare move.

sentences.zh: 憲宗賞其功，授潞府左司馬，遷懷州刺史，兼充河陽三城節度使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong rewarded his merit, appointed him Left Assistant Administrator of the Lu prefecture, transferred him to prefect of Huai, and concurrently made him military commissioner of Heyang's three cities.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong rewarded him with the post of Left Assistant Administrator at Lu, then prefect of Huai and military commissioner of the Heyang Three Cities.

sentences.zh: 會討淮、蔡，用重胤壓境，仍割汝州隸河陽。

translations.literal: When the campaign against Huai and Cai began, Chongyin was used to press the border, and Ruzhou was detached and placed under Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huai-Cai campaign he was stationed to pin the enemy border, and Ruzhou was reassigned to his Heyang command.

sentences.zh: 自王師討淮西三年，重胤與李光顏掎角相應，大小百余戰，以至元濟誅。

translations.literal: From the three years the imperial army campaigned in Huai-Xi, Chongyin and Li Guangyan coordinated in pincer fashion, fighting more than a hundred engagements large and small, until Yuanji was executed.
translations.idiomatic: For the three years of the Huai-Xi war Chongyin and Li Guangyan fought in mutual support through more than a hundred battles, until Wu Yuanji was captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 就加檢校尚書右僕射，轉司空。

translations.literal: He was then additionally made acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting Right Vice Director of State and then Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 蔡將有李端者，過溵河降重胤。

translations.literal: Among the Cai generals was one Li Duan, who crossed the Shen River and surrendered to Chongyin.
translations.idiomatic: A rebel general named Li Duan crossed the Shen River to surrender to Chongyin.

sentences.zh: 其妻為賊束縛於樹，臠食至死，將絕，猶呼其夫曰：「善事烏僕射。」

translations.literal: His wife was bound to a tree by the rebels and cut apart piece by piece until she died; on the verge of death she still called to her husband, saying, "Serve Vice Director Wu well."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels bound his wife to a tree and cut her apart piece by piece until she died. With her last breath she still called to her husband: "Serve Vice Director Wu well."

sentences.zh: 其得人心如此。

translations.literal: Such was the depth of the devotion he inspired.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the devotion he inspired in others.

sentences.zh: 元和十三年，代鄭權為橫海軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yuanhe he replaced Zheng Quan as military commissioner of the Henghai army.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 13 he replaced Zheng Quan as military commissioner of Henghai.

sentences.zh: 既至鎮，上言曰：「臣以河朔能拒朝命者，其大略可見。

translations.literal: After reaching his post he memorialized, saying, "Your servant holds that the general pattern by which Hebei has been able to defy the court's orders is clear.
translations.idiomatic: After taking command he memorialized the throne: "The reason Hebei has defied the court for so long is not hard to see.

sentences.zh: 蓋刺史失其職，反使鎮將領兵事。

translations.literal: It is that prefects lost their proper duties, and garrison commanders instead took charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects have lost their proper roles, and garrison commanders hold military power instead.

sentences.zh: 若刺史各得職分，又有鎮兵，則節將雖有祿山、思明之奸，豈能據一州為叛哉？

translations.literal: If each prefect exercised his proper duties and garrison troops were also present, then even if a military commissioner had the treachery of a Lu Shan or Shi Siming, how could he hold a single prefecture in rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: If every prefect did his proper job and garrison troops remained under separate command, not even a commander with the treachery of An Lushan or Shi Siming could rebel from a single prefecture.

sentences.zh: 所以河朔六十年能拒朝命者，只以奪刺史、縣令之職，自作威福故也。

translations.literal: The reason Hebei was able to defy the court for sixty years is solely that those posts seized the duties of prefects and county magistrates and made law and favor for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei resisted the throne for sixty years only because military commissioners stripped prefects and magistrates of their authority and ruled as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 臣所管德、棣、景三州，已舉公牒，各還刺史職事訖，應在州兵，並令刺史收管。

translations.literal: The three prefectures De, Di, and Jing under my jurisdiction have already received official notices restoring each prefect's duties; all troops stationed in those prefectures are ordered to be placed under prefectural control.
translations.idiomatic: In the three prefectures under my command—De, Di, and Jing—I have already issued orders restoring each prefect to his proper duties and placing all local troops under prefectural authority.

sentences.zh: 又景州本是弓高縣，請卻廢為縣，歸化縣本是草市，請廢縣依舊屬德州。」

translations.literal: Further, Jing Prefecture was originally Gonggao County—I request it be abolished and restored to county status; Guihua County was originally a market settlement—I request the county be abolished and returned to Dezhou's jurisdiction as before."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Prefecture was originally Gonggao County and should be demoted back to a county. Guihua County began as a market town and should be abolished and returned to De Prefecture as before."

sentences.zh: 詔並從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 由是法制修立，各歸名分。

translations.literal: Thereby the laws and institutions were set in order and each office returned to its proper place.
translations.idiomatic: From then on authority was clarified and every office held its proper place.

sentences.zh: 及屯軍深州，重胤以朝廷制置失宜，賊方憑淩，未可輕進，觀望累月。

translations.literal: When he encamped at Shenzhou, Chongyin held that the court's dispositions were ill judged—the rebels were pressing aggressively and one should not advance rashly—and he held back for many months.
translations.idiomatic: When stationed at Shenzhou, Chongyin judged the court's strategy unsound. The rebels were on the offensive and he refused to risk a rash advance, waiting for months.

sentences.zh: 穆宗急於誅叛，遂以杜叔良代之，以重胤檢校司徒，兼興元尹，充山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: Muzong, eager to punish the rebels, replaced him with Du Shuliang; Chongyin was made acting Grand Preceptor, concurrently Governor of Xingyuan, and military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Eager to crush the rebels, Muzong replaced him with Du Shuliang and reassigned Chongyin as acting Grand Preceptor, governor of Xingyuan, and military commissioner of Shannan West.

sentences.zh: 召至京師，復以本官為天平軍節度、鄆曹濮等州觀察等使。

translations.literal: Summoned to the capital, he was again appointed with his existing rank as military commissioner of Tianping and overseer of Yan, Cao, Pu, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital, he was soon sent out again as military commissioner of Tianping and inspector-general of Yan, Cao, Pu, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 李同捷據滄州，請襲父位，朝廷不從。

translations.literal: Li Tongjie held Cangzhou and requested to succeed his father's position; the court did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tongjie held Cangzhou and asked to inherit his father's post; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 議者慮狡童拒命，欲以重臣代。

translations.literal: Those deliberating feared the cunning youth would defy orders and wished to replace him with a senior minister.
translations.idiomatic: Officials feared the young rebel would resist and wanted a senior commander in his place.

sentences.zh: 乃移鎮兗海，加太子太師、平章事，俾兼領滄景節度，仍舊割齊州隸之，蓋望不勞師而底定。

translations.literal: He was therefore transferred to Yanhai, elevated to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and Grand Councillor, and ordered to hold concurrently the Cang-Jing command; Qi Prefecture was again detached to his jurisdiction, in the hope the matter might be settled without troubling the army.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to Yanhai, made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and Grand Councillor, and given concurrent command of Cang-Jing with Qi Prefecture attached—hoping the rebellion could be settled without a major campaign.

sentences.zh: 制出旬日，重胤卒，贈太尉。

translations.literal: Within ten days of the edict Chongyin died and was posthumously made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days of the appointment Chongyin died and was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 重胤出自行間，及為長帥，赤心奉上。

translations.literal: Chongyin had risen from the ranks; once a chief commander, he served the throne with a loyal heart.
translations.idiomatic: Raised from the ranks, he served the throne with wholehearted loyalty once he held high command.

sentences.zh: 能與下同甘苦，所至立功，未嘗矜伐。

translations.literal: He could share hardship and ease with those below him; wherever he went he achieved merit and never boastfully claimed credit.
translations.idiomatic: He shared hardship and comfort with his men, won victories wherever he was posted, and never trumpeted his own glory.

sentences.zh: 而善待賓寮，禮分同至，當時名士，鹹願依之。

translations.literal: Moreover he treated his staff generously and extended equal courtesy to all; eminent men of the time all wished to attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: He treated his staff with genuine respect and equal courtesy, and leading scholars of the day sought to serve under him.

sentences.zh: 身歿之日，軍士二十余人，皆割股肉以為祭酹，雖古之名將，無以加焉。

translations.literal: On the day of his death more than twenty soldiers cut flesh from their thighs as sacrificial offerings; even the famed generals of antiquity could not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died more than twenty soldiers cut flesh from their own thighs as funeral offerings—a devotion unmatched even among the great generals of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 子漢弘嗣，起復授左領軍衛將軍。

translations.literal: His son Han Hongsi, recalled from mourning, was appointed General of the Left Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Han Hongsi was recalled from mourning and made a general of the Left Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 漢弘上表乞終服紀，文宗嘉詔從之。

translations.literal: Han Hong memorialized asking to complete the mourning period; Emperor Wenzong approved and granted the request.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hong petitioned to finish his mourning period properly; Emperor Wenzong praised his filial conduct and agreed.

sentences.zh: 服闋，方授官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was then given office.
translations.idiomatic: Only after his mourning ended was he formally appointed.

sentences.zh: 王沛，許州人。

translations.literal: Wang Pei was a native of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pei was a native of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 年十八，有勇決。

translations.literal: At eighteen he was bold and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he was already bold and decisive.

sentences.zh: 許州節度使上官涚奇其才，以女妻之，署為牙門將。

translations.literal: Xuzhou military commissioner Shangguan Shuo admired his talent, gave him his daughter in marriage, and appointed him a garrison gate officer.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Shuo, military commissioner of Xuzhou, admired his ability, married him to his daughter, and made him a garrison officer.

sentences.zh: 及涚卒，子婿田偁迫脅涚子，欲邀襲位，懼監軍使不順其事，將結謀伏兵以圖之。

translations.literal: When Shuo died, his son-in-law Tian Cheng coerced Shuo's son, intending to seize the command by inheritance; fearing the army supervisor would not go along, he plotted to ambush him with hidden troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuo died, his son-in-law Tian Cheng threatened Shuo's son and tried to seize the command. Fearing the army supervisor would block him, he planned an ambush.

sentences.zh: 沛竊知其謀，密告監軍，因盡擒其黨於伏匿之所。

translations.literal: Pei secretly learned of the plot, privately informed the army supervisor, and thereby seized the whole faction in their hiding place.
translations.idiomatic: Pei learned of the plot in secret, warned the army supervisor, and all the conspirators were arrested at their hideout.

sentences.zh: 監軍範日用以其事聞，德宗乃以陳許行軍司馬劉昌裔總統其軍，賜沛手詔，令護涚之子赴上都。

translations.literal: Army supervisor Fan Riyong reported the matter; Emperor Dezong then put Chen-Xu marching chief Liu Changyi in overall command of the army, bestowed a handwritten edict on Pei, and ordered him to escort Shuo's son to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor Fan Riyong reported the affair. Dezong placed Liu Changyi in command of the Chen-Xu forces, sent Pei a personal edict, and ordered him to escort Shuo's son to the capital.

sentences.zh: 既至，召見，德宗謂之曰：「據卿忠義，寵宜加等。

translations.literal: After arriving he was summoned to audience; Dezong said to him, "Judging by your loyalty and righteousness, favor should be increased in rank.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived at court, Dezong told him, "Your loyalty deserves a far greater reward.

sentences.zh: 但昌裔所奏，只請加監察御史，朕意殊為不足。

translations.literal: But what Changyi memorialized requested only promotion to Investigatory Censor; in Our opinion that is quite insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: But Changyi's memorial asked only for Investigatory Censor—a rank far below what you deserve.

sentences.zh: 卿速歸，便宣付昌裔，更令奏來。」

translations.literal: You should return quickly, convey this on Our authority to Changyi, and have him submit anew."
translations.idiomatic: Return at once, tell Changyi on my authority to send up a new recommendation."

sentences.zh: 遂驛騎而還。

translations.literal: He then returned by post-horse relay.
translations.idiomatic: He then rode post-haste back.

sentences.zh: 未至許州，拜開府儀同三司、兼御史中丞，依前本職。

translations.literal: Before reaching Xuzhou he was appointed Kaifu Yitong Sansi and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, retaining his previous post.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached Xuzhou he was promoted to Kaifu Yitong Sansi and Censor-in-Chief while keeping his existing duties.

sentences.zh: 吳元濟反，李光顏受命攻討，奇沛節概，署行營兵馬使，別統勁兵屯於近郊。

translations.literal: When Wu Yuanji rebelled, Li Guangyan received orders to attack and campaign; admiring Pei's moral bearing, he appointed him forward-camp horse-and-troop commissioner and separately commanded crack troops encamped in the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yuanji rose in rebellion, Li Guangyan was tasked with suppressing him. Impressed by Pei's character, he made him camp cavalry commander with elite troops stationed in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 及軍合，連破蔡寇。

translations.literal: When the armies joined, they repeatedly defeated Cai rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Once the armies united they routed the rebels again and again.

sentences.zh: 頻詔進軍，諸將觀望，無敢先渡溵河。

translations.literal: Repeated edicts ordered advance; the generals looked on hesitantly, and none dared cross the Shen River first.
translations.idiomatic: Edict after edict ordered them forward, but the generals hung back—none dared cross the Shen River first.

sentences.zh: 沛率兵五千，夜渡溵河合流口，徑扼賊喉而成城。

translations.literal: Pei led five thousand troops, crossed by night at the Shen River's confluence, seized the rebels' vital throat directly, and built a fortified camp.
translations.idiomatic: Pei took five thousand men across the Shen River by night at its confluence, seized the critical chokepoint, and fortified a camp there.

sentences.zh: 自是，河陽、宣武、太原、魏博等軍繼渡，掎角進攻郾城。

translations.literal: From then on the armies of Heyang, Xuanwu, Taiyuan, Weibo, and others crossed in succession and advanced on Yancheng in coordinated pincer.
translations.idiomatic: After that the armies of Heyang, Xuanwu, Taiyuan, Weibo, and others crossed in turn and pressed on Yancheng in concert.

sentences.zh: 沛先結壘與賊對，賊將鄧懷金率眾面縛而降。

translations.literal: Pei first built ramparts facing the rebels; rebel general Deng Huaijin led his force with hands bound in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Pei built fortifications face-to-face with the enemy; rebel general Deng Huaijin came forward bound in surrender.

sentences.zh: 蔡賊平。

translations.literal: The Cai rebels were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Cai rebellion was crushed.

sentences.zh: 沛隨李光顏入朝，光顏具陳沛功，加御史大夫。

translations.literal: Pei followed Li Guangyan to court; Guangyan fully reported Pei's merit, and he was promoted to Chief Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Pei accompanied Li Guangyan to court. Guangyan laid out his achievements in full, and Pei was made Chief Censor.

sentences.zh: 既還鎮，光顏受詔討鄆寇。

translations.literal: After returning to his command, Guangyan received orders to campaign against Yan rebels.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to his post, Guangyan was ordered to campaign against the Yan rebels.

sentences.zh: 及李師道誅，詔分許州兵戍於邠，以沛為都將，救鹽州，擊退吐蕃。

translations.literal: When Li Shidao was executed, an edict divided Xuzhou troops to garrison at Bin; Pei was made chief commander, rescued Yizhou, and repelled the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Shidao was killed, Xuzhou troops were sent to garrison Bin; Pei was put in overall command, relieved Yizhou, and drove back the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 以功加寧州刺史，遷陳州。

translations.literal: For his merit he was additionally appointed Prefect of Ningzhou and transferred to Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his service he was made Prefect of Ningzhou and transferred to Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 李絺反，詔沛兼忠武節度副使，率師討絺。

translations.literal: Li Chi rebelled; an edict appointed Pei concurrently as deputy military commissioner of Zhongwu and ordered him to lead troops to suppress Chi.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chi rose in rebellion, the throne named Pei deputy military commissioner of Zhongwu and sent him to lead an expedition against Chi.

sentences.zh: 絺平，加檢校右散騎常侍，遷兗海沂密節度、觀察等使。

translations.literal: When Chi was pacified, Pei was promoted to acting Right Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders and transferred to military commissioner and surveillance commissioner of Yan-Hai-Yi-Mi.
translations.idiomatic: After Chi was subdued, Pei received the acting title of Right Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders and was posted as military commissioner and surveillance commissioner of Yan-Hai-Yi-Mi.

sentences.zh: 此邦新造，人情獷驁，沛明申法令，選蒐軍政，期年大理。

translations.literal: This region had only recently been established; the people were fiercely unruly. Pei clearly enforced the laws, selected and inspected military and civil affairs, and within a year order was greatly restored.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit was newly formed and its people rough and defiant. Pei made the laws plain, tightened military and civil administration, and within a year the region was well governed.

sentences.zh: 明年，改檢校工部尚書，充忠武軍節度、陳許蔡觀察等使。

translations.literal: The next year he was reassigned as acting Minister of Works and appointed military commissioner of Zhongwu Army and surveillance commissioner of Chen-Xu-Cai.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made acting Minister of Works and took up the posts of Zhongwu military commissioner and Chen-Xu-Cai surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 卒於鎮，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: He died in his post; posthumously he was given the title of Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died at his command; the court posthumously honored him as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 子逢。

translations.literal: His son was Feng.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Feng.

sentences.zh: 逢，少沈勇，從父征伐有功，為忠武都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Feng in youth was steadfast and brave; following his father on campaigns he won merit and became chief military affairs officer of Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was quiet and resolute from youth. He followed his father on campaign, earned distinction, and became Zhongwu's chief military affairs officer.

sentences.zh: 太和中，入宿衛，歷諸衛將軍。

translations.literal: During the Taihe era he entered palace guard service and successively held generalships in the guard units.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe reign he joined the palace guards and rose through the guard generalships.

sentences.zh: 從石雄、劉沔破回紇於天德。

translations.literal: He followed Shi Xiong and Liu Mian in defeating the Uyghurs at Tiande.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Shi Xiong and Liu Mian when they routed the Uyghurs at Tiande.

sentences.zh: 性果決，用法嚴。

translations.literal: His nature was resolute and decisive; he applied the law strictly.
translations.idiomatic: He was decisive by temperament and enforced discipline without leniency.

sentences.zh: 其時有二千人不上陣，官賜賞給，逢皆不與。

translations.literal: At that time two thousand men had not taken the field; the office issued rewards and grants, but Feng gave them none.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand soldiers had never entered battle, yet the command issued them rewards and stipends; Feng refused to grant any of it.

sentences.zh: 或非之，逢曰：「健兒向前冒白刃，若無功而賞，其如冒刃者何？」

translations.literal: Some criticized this; Feng said, "Brave soldiers charge forward facing naked blades—if the idle are rewarded without merit, what becomes of those who risked the blades?"
translations.idiomatic: When others objected, Feng said, "Men who face naked steel deserve credit—if the absent are rewarded without merit, what honor is left for those who risked their lives?"

sentences.zh: 王宰攻劉稹，逢領陳許七千人屯翼城，代田令昭。

translations.literal: Wang Zai attacked Liu Zhen; Feng led seven thousand troops from Chen-Xu to encamp at Yicheng, replacing Tian Lingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zai moved against Liu Zhen, Feng took seven thousand Chen-Xu troops to Yicheng, relieving Tian Lingzhao.

sentences.zh: 賊平，檢校左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was appointed acting Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed he was made acting Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders.

sentences.zh: 累遷至忠武軍節度、陳許觀察等使。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted until he became military commissioner of Zhongwu Army and surveillance commissioner of Chen-Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments until he held the Zhongwu military commission and the Chen-Xu surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 李珙，山東甲姓，代修婚姻。

translations.literal: Li Gong—Li Gong was of a premier Shandong clan, with generations of marriage alliances.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gong came from one of Shandong's foremost clans, a line that had maintained marriage ties for generations.

sentences.zh: 至珙，不好讀書，唯以弓馬為務。

translations.literal: By Gong's generation they no longer cared for books and devoted themselves only to bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: By Gong's time the family had lost interest in study and cared only for archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 長六尺余，氣貌魁岸。

translations.literal: He stood over six feet tall, with an imposing build and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He stood more than six feet tall, with a towering frame and commanding presence.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣澤潞謁李抱真，異之，將選為衙門將，旋以酒酣使氣，復欲棄之。

translations.literal: Once when he went to Zelu to visit Li Baozhen, Baozhen found him remarkable and was about to choose him as a gate commander, but then when drunk Gong showed a domineering temper, and Baozhen again wished to cast him aside.
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to Li Baozhen in Zelu, Baozhen was impressed and meant to make him a gate commander, but after wine Gong's arrogant temper surfaced and Baozhen again wanted to discard him.

sentences.zh: 都將王虔休謂抱真曰：「李珙，奇士也，若不能用，不如殺之，無為他人所得。」

translations.literal: Commander Wang Qianxiu said to Baozhen, "Li Gong is an extraordinary man; if you cannot use him, you would do better to kill him than let another gain him."
translations.idiomatic: Commander Wang Qianxiu told Baozhen, "Li Gong is no ordinary man. If you will not employ him, kill him rather than let a rival take him."

sentences.zh: 抱真死，虔休為帥，乃依虔休，累為昭義大將。

translations.literal: When Baozhen died and Qianxiu became commander, Gong attached himself to Qianxiu and rose through the ranks to become a great general of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: After Baozhen's death Qianxiu took command; Gong entered his service and eventually became a senior general of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 吐突承璀之擒盧從史，烏重胤實預其謀，珙初不知，將救從史。

translations.literal: When Tutu Chenghuan captured Lu Congshi, Wu Chongyin had actually taken part in the plot; Gong did not know this at first and was about to rescue Congshi.
translations.idiomatic: When Tutu Chenghuan seized Lu Congshi, Wu Chongyin had been party to the scheme. Gong knew nothing of this at first and was preparing to rescue Congshi.

sentences.zh: 聞重胤受朝旨，乃觀望不進，重胤以此德之。

translations.literal: Learning that Chongyin had received the court's orders, he held back and did not advance; Chongyin was grateful to him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Once he learned that Chongyin was acting on imperial orders, he halted and did not move forward; Chongyin counted it a debt of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 後領河陽，乃置於麾下。

translations.literal: Later, when Chongyin took command of Heyang, he placed Gong under his command.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongyin later assumed command at Heyang, he kept Gong in his own ranks.

sentences.zh: 然朝廷以與從史厚善，竟出為北邊一校。

translations.literal: But the court, considering Gong's close friendship with Congshi, in the end posted him as a mere frontier company commander in the north.
translations.idiomatic: The court, however, distrusted his close ties to Congshi and finally reduced him to a frontier company commander in the north.

sentences.zh: 元和十年，征淮西，重胤懇表為諸道行營都虞候，詔特從之，俄以母憂去職。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yuanhe, when the Huai West campaign was launched, Chongyin earnestly memorialized that Gong be made chief adjutant of the multi-route forward camp; an edict specially granted this, but soon afterward Gong left office on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 10, as the Huai West expedition began, Chongyin urgently petitioned to have Gong named chief adjutant of the combined forward camp. The throne granted the request, but Gong soon left his post to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除右武衛上將軍。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed senior general of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he was appointed senior general of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 長慶四年八月卒，年六十四，廢朝一日。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Changqing he died at age sixty-four; the court suspended audience for one day.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of Changqing 4, aged sixty-four; the court closed audience for a day in mourning.

sentences.zh: 李祐，本蔡州牙將。

translations.literal: Li You—Li You was originally a yamen general of Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li You had begun as a staff general in Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 事吳元濟，驍勇善戰。

translations.literal: He served Wu Yuanji and was fierce, brave, and skilled in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He served Wu Yuanji and was renowned for ferocity, courage, and battlefield skill.

sentences.zh: 自王師討淮西，祐為行營將，每抗官軍，皆憚之。

translations.literal: From the time the imperial army campaigned against Huai West, You served as a forward-camp general; each time he resisted the government forces, they feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Once the imperial armies marched on Huai West, You commanded in the rebel forward camp, and every force that met him learned to dread him.

sentences.zh: 元和十二年，為李愬所擒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanhe he was captured by Li Su.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 12 he was taken prisoner by Li Su.

sentences.zh: 愬知祐有膽略，釋其死，厚遇之。

translations.literal: Su knew that You had courage and strategic talent, spared his life, and treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Su saw that You had both nerve and strategic gifts, spared his life, and treated him with marked favor.

sentences.zh: 推誠定分，與同寢食，往往帳中密語，達曙不寐。

translations.literal: He treated him with complete sincerity and fixed his status, sharing bed and board with him; often they would speak privately in the tent until dawn without sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: Su won his trust outright, settled his standing, and shared his quarters and meals. Often they talked alone in the tent until dawn without sleep.

sentences.zh: 人有耳屬於外者，但屢聞祐感泣聲。

translations.literal: Those listening outside heard You weeping with emotion again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone listening outside the tent could hear You weeping again and again, overcome with feeling.

sentences.zh: 而軍中以前時為祐殺傷者多，營壘諸卒會議，皆恨不殺祐。

translations.literal: But in the army many had been killed or wounded by You in earlier fighting; the soldiers in the camps met in assembly and all regretted that You had not been killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet many in the army had been killed or maimed by You in earlier battles, and when the camps met in council the men cursed the fact that he still lived.

sentences.zh: 愬以眾情歸怨，慮不能全，因送祐於京師，乃上表救之。

translations.literal: Su, seeing the soldiers' animosity and fearing he could not protect You, therefore sent You to the capital and submitted a memorial pleading for his life.
translations.idiomatic: Su saw the hatred gathering against You and feared he could not keep him safe, so he sent You to the capital and memorialized the throne to spare him.

sentences.zh: 憲宗特恕，遂遣祐賜愬。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong specially pardoned him and sent You back to Su as a gift from the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong granted a special pardon and returned You to Su as an imperial gift.

sentences.zh: 愬大喜，即以三千精兵付之。

translations.literal: Su was overjoyed and immediately entrusted three thousand elite troops to him.
translations.idiomatic: Su was elated and at once placed three thousand picked troops under his command.

sentences.zh: 祐聽言，無有所疑，竟以祐破蔡，擒元濟。

translations.literal: Su took him at his word without the slightest doubt, and in the end with You's help broke through at Cai and captured Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: Su trusted him completely, and in the end it was You who helped him storm Cai and seize Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 以功授神武將軍，遷金吾將軍、檢校左散騎常侍、夏州刺史、御史大夫、夏綏銀宥節度使。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed General of the Divine Martial Guard, then promoted to Jinwu General, acting Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, Prefect of Xiazhou, Chief Censor, and military commissioner of Xia-Sui-Yin-You.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was made General of the Divine Martial Guard, then Jinwu General, acting Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, Prefect of Xiazhou, Chief Censor, and military commissioner of Xia-Sui-Yin-You.

sentences.zh: 寶歷初，入為右金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoli he entered court service as senior general of the Right Jinwu Guard.
