translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Baoli reign he entered the capital as senior general of the Right Jinwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 尋以吐蕃入寇，出為涇州刺史、涇原節度使。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, when the Tibetans invaded, he was sent out as Prefect of Jingzhou and military commissioner of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans raided soon after, he was dispatched as Prefect of Jingzhou and military commissioner of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 太和初，討李同捷，遷檢校戶部尚書、滄州刺史、滄德景節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, during the campaign against Li Tongjie, he was transferred to acting Minister of Revenue, Prefect of Cangzhou, and military commissioner of Cang-De-Jing.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taihe, while campaigning against Li Tongjie, he was made acting Minister of Revenue, Prefect of Cangzhou, and military commissioner of Cang-De-Jing.

sentences.zh: 太和三年五月卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Taihe he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month of Taihe 3.

sentences.zh: 董重質，本淮西牙將，吳少誠之子婿也。

translations.literal: Dong Chongzhi—Dong Chongzhi was originally a Huai West yamen general and son-in-law of Wu Shaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chongzhi had been a Huai West staff general and was married to a daughter of Wu Shaocheng.

sentences.zh: 性勇悍，識軍機，善用兵。

translations.literal: He was by nature fierce and bold; he understood military circumstances and was skilled in the use of troops.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce and bold by nature, he read battlefield conditions well and handled troops expertly.

sentences.zh: 及元濟拒命，重質又為謀主，領大軍當王師，連歲不拔，皆重質之謀也。

translations.literal: When Yuanji defied the throne, Chongzhi again became chief strategist; leading the main army he blocked the imperial forces, and for years they could not prevail—all due to Chongzhi's stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanji defied the court, Chongzhi again became his chief strategist. He led the main rebel force against the imperial armies, and for years they could not break him—chiefly because of his plans.

sentences.zh: 元和十二年，宰相裴度督兵淮西，至郾城，元濟乃悉發左右及守城之卒，委重質而拒度。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanhe, Chief Minister Pei Du directed the Huai West campaign and reached Yancheng; Yuanji then sent out all his personal guards and garrison troops, entrusting them to Chongzhi to resist Du.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 12, when Chief Minister Pei Du took command of the Huai West campaign and advanced to Yancheng, Yuanji committed his entire household guard and garrison to Chongzhi to hold Du at bay.

sentences.zh: 時李愬乘虛入蔡。

translations.literal: At that time Li Su seized the opening and entered Cai.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Li Su slipped through the gap and entered Cai.

sentences.zh: 既擒元濟，重質之家在蔡，愬乃安恤之，仍使其子持書禮以召重質。

translations.literal: After Yuanji was captured, Chongzhi's family was in Cai; Su comforted and provided for them, and had Chongzhi's son carry a letter of invitation to summon Chongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuanji was taken, Su saw to Chongzhi's family still in Cai, reassured and supplied them, and sent Chongzhi's son with a letter inviting him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 重質見其子，知城已陷，及元濟囚窘之狀，乃慨然以單騎歸愬，白衣叩伏。

translations.literal: When Chongzhi saw his son, he learned the city had fallen and saw Yuanji's imprisoned plight; sighing deeply, he returned alone on horseback to Su and prostrated himself in common dress.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongzhi met his son he learned the city was lost and saw Yuanji in chains. With a deep sigh he rode alone back to Su and prostrated himself in plain clothes.

sentences.zh: 愬揖登階，以賓禮與之食。

translations.literal: Su bowed him up the steps and entertained him with the courtesy due a guest.
translations.idiomatic: Su raised him with a bow, led him up the steps, and received him with full guest honors at table.

sentences.zh: 憲宗欲殺之，愬奏許以不死而來降，請免之，且乞於本軍驅使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong wished to execute him; Su memorialized that Chongzhi had come to surrender relying on a pledge of life, asked that he be spared, and requested that he be kept for service in his own army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong wanted him put to death, but Su argued that Chongzhi had surrendered on a promise of life, pleaded for clemency, and asked to keep him under command in his own army.

sentences.zh: 於是，貶春州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was demoted to registrar of Chunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore demoted to registrar of Chunzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，轉太子少詹事，委武寧軍收管驅使，仍加金紫。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, placed under the Wuning Army for supervision and employment, and further granted gold and purple insignia.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, assigned to the Wuning Army for supervised service, and given gold and purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 十五年，征入，授左神武軍將軍，知軍事，兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was recalled to court and appointed general of the Left Divine Martial Army with command of its affairs, concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was recalled and appointed general of the Left Divine Martial Army with operational command, concurrently Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 仍賜金帛，與有功者等。

translations.literal: He was also granted gold and silk, equal to those who had rendered merit.
translations.idiomatic: He also received gold and silk on the same scale as the men who had earned distinction in the campaign.

sentences.zh: 尋授鹽州刺史，又遷左右神策及諸道劍南西川行營節度使、檢校左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Prefect of Yanzhou, then transferred to military commissioner of the Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies and the multi-route Xichuan forward camp, with the acting title of Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Prefect of Yanzhou, then military commissioner of the Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies and the multi-route Xichuan forward camp, with the acting title of Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，又轉夏綏銀宥節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe he was again transferred to military commissioner of Xia-Sui-Yin-You.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 4 he was transferred again to the Xia-Sui-Yin-You military commission.

sentences.zh: 五年，就加檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he received the additional title of acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was further granted the acting title of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 重質訓兵立法，羌戎畏服。

translations.literal: Chongzhi trained the troops and established regulations; the Qiang and Rong submitted in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi drilled the army and set firm regulations, and the Qiang and Rong peoples submitted in awe.

sentences.zh: 八年八月卒，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the eighth year he died; posthumously he was given the title of Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of the eighth year and was posthumously honored as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 楊元卿，祖子華，德州安陵縣丞。

translations.literal: Yang Yuanqing—Yang Yuanqing's grandfather Zihua was assistant magistrate of Anling County in Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuanqing's grandfather Zihua had served as assistant magistrate of Anling County in Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 父寓，申州鐘山縣令。

translations.literal: His father Yu was magistrate of Zhongshan County in Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu had been magistrate of Zhongshan County in Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 元卿少孤，慷慨有才略。

translations.literal: Yuanqing was orphaned young; he was high-spirited and possessed talent and strategic ability.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing lost his parents early. He was ardent in temperament and gifted with talent and strategic insight.

sentences.zh: 及冠，尚漂蕩江嶺之表，縱遊放言，人謂之狂生。

translations.literal: Upon reaching adulthood he still drifted about the Jiang-Ling region, roaming freely and speaking unrestrainedly; people called him a wild scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Even after coming of age he wandered the Jiang-Ling frontier, roaming freely and speaking without restraint, and people called him a reckless young man.

sentences.zh: 時吳少誠專蔡州，朝廷姑息之。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Shaocheng held exclusive control of Caizhou, and the court treated him with indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaocheng then held Caizhou in his own hand, and the court indulged him.

sentences.zh: 元卿白衣謁見，署以劇縣，旋辟為從事，奏授試大理評事。

translations.literal: Yuanqing visited him in plain dress; Shaocheng assigned him a demanding county and soon recruited him as a staff officer, memorializing the court to grant him provisional status as an evaluator in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing presented himself in plain clothes. Shaocheng gave him a difficult county post, then took him onto staff and memorialized the court to grant him provisional rank as an evaluator in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 亦事少陽，後奏轉監察裏行。

translations.literal: He also served Wu Shaoyang and was later memorialized for transfer to acting censor.
translations.idiomatic: He later served Wu Shaoyang as well and was memorialized for appointment as acting censor.

sentences.zh: 因上奏，宰相李吉甫深加慰納，自是一歲或再隨奏至京師。

translations.literal: Through his memorials to court, Chief Minister Li Jifu warmly welcomed and accepted him; from then on once or twice a year he would accompany memorials to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials reached Chief Minister Li Jifu, who received him warmly; thereafter he traveled to the capital once or twice a year with dispatches.

sentences.zh: 元卿每與少陽言，諭以大義。

translations.literal: Yuanqing often spoke with Shaoyang, instructing him in the greater right.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing often urged Shaoyang toward the larger obligations of loyalty to the throne.

sentences.zh: 乃為兇黨所構，賴節度判官蘇肇保持，故免。

translations.literal: He was then framed by the villainous faction; only because the military commissioner's administrative assistant Su Zhao protected him did he escape harm.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel hard-liners then plotted against him, and he survived only because the commissioner's aide Su Zhao shielded him.

sentences.zh: 元卿潛奉朝廷，內耗少陽之事。

translations.literal: In secret Yuanqing served the court, undermining Shaoyang's affairs from within.
translations.idiomatic: In secret he served the court, weakening Shaoyang's position from within.

sentences.zh: 及少陽死，其子元濟繼立。

translations.literal: When Shaoyang died, his son Yuanji succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyang died, his son Yuanji took his place.

sentences.zh: 元卿說曰：「先尚書性吝，諸將皆饑寒。

translations.literal: Yuanqing persuaded him, saying, "Your late father was miserly by nature; all the generals are hungry and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing urged him, saying, "Your late father was tight-fisted by nature, and the generals are starving and freezing.

sentences.zh: 今須布惠以自固也。

translations.literal: Now you must distribute bounty to secure your own position.
translations.idiomatic: You must now spread largesse if you mean to hold their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 府中有無，元卿熟知之，曷若散聘諸道，卑辭厚禮，以丈人行呼群帥，庶幾一助，而諸將大獲矣。

translations.literal: I know exactly what the command has and does not have—why not send envoys to every circuit with humble words and lavish gifts, address the various commanders as elders, and with even a little help the generals would gain greatly.
translations.idiomatic: I know the command's coffers inside out. Why not send envoys to every circuit with humble words and rich gifts, address the other commanders as elders, and with even modest aid your officers would profit handsomely?

sentences.zh: 元卿願將留後表上聞，朝廷安得不從哉？」

translations.literal: I am willing to carry the posthumous memorial reporting the matter to court—how could the court refuse?"
translations.idiomatic: Let me carry the acting-commissioner's memorial to court—surely the throne will not refuse."

sentences.zh: 元濟許之。

translations.literal: Yuanji agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji agreed.

sentences.zh: 元卿即日離蔡，以賊勢盈虛條奏，潛請詔諸道拘留使者。

translations.literal: That same day Yuanqing left Cai, submitted a detailed report on the rebels' strength and weakness, and secretly requested an edict that each circuit detain the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Yuanqing quit Cai, sent the court a detailed accounting of rebel strength and weakness, and secretly asked that the circuits detain Yuanji's envoys.

sentences.zh: 及元濟覺，元卿妻陳氏並四男並為元濟所殺，同圬一射垛。

translations.literal: When Yuanji realized what had happened, Yuanqing's wife Lady Chen and his four sons were all killed by Yuanji and buried together in one mound for archery butts.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanji discovered the betrayal, he killed Yuanqing's wife Lady Chen and all four of his sons and buried them together in a single execution mound.

sentences.zh: 蘇肇以保持元卿，亦同日被害。

translations.literal: Su Zhao, because he had protected Yuanqing, was killed on the same day as well.
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhao, who had shielded Yuanqing, was killed that same day.

sentences.zh: 詔授元卿嶽王府司馬，尋遷太子僕射。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yuanqing marshal of the Prince of Yue's household; soon he was promoted to Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: The throne appointed Yuanqing marshal of the Prince of Yue's household, then soon promoted him to Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 元和十三年，授蔡州刺史、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yuanhe he was appointed Prefect of Caizhou, concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 13 he was named Prefect of Caizhou and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 未行，改授光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Before he set out, the appointment was changed to Vice Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, the appointment was changed to Vice Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 初，朝廷比令元卿與李愬會議，於唐州東境選要便處，權置行蔡州。

translations.literal: Initially the court had ordered Yuanqing to confer with Li Su and, on the eastern border of Tangzhou, select a strategic location where a provisional Xing Caizhou would be established.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court had ordered Yuanqing to meet with Li Su and, on Tangzhou's eastern frontier, choose a strategic site for a provisional seat of Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 如百姓官健有歸順者，便準敕優恤，必令全活。

translations.literal: If civilians or soldiers wished to submit, they were to be favored and cared for according to the edict, and their lives were to be fully preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Any civilians or troops who came over were to receive the generous treatment prescribed by edict, with their lives fully protected.

sentences.zh: 既而召見，元卿遽奏請借度支錢，及言事頗多不合旨。

translations.literal: When he was summoned for audience, Yuanqing immediately memorialized to borrow funds from the Treasury, and much of what he said was at odds with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned to court, Yuanqing at once asked to borrow Treasury funds, and much of what he said ran against the emperor's wishes.

sentences.zh: 宰相裴度亦以諸將討賊三年，功成在旦暮，如更分土地與元卿，即恐相侵生事，故罷前命而改授焉。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Pei Du also reasoned that the generals had been campaigning against the rebels for three years and success was imminent; if more territory were now given to Yuanqing, it might lead to encroachment and trouble—therefore the previous order was revoked and he was given a different appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Pei Du also argued that after three years of campaigning victory was near; granting Yuanqing fresh territory now would only invite rivalry and disorder. The earlier order was therefore withdrawn and a new appointment made.

sentences.zh: 是歲，既平淮西，元卿奏曰：「淮西甚有寶貨及犀帶，臣知之，往取必得。」

translations.literal: That year, after Huai West was pacified, Yuanqing memorialized, saying, "Huai West holds great stores of valuables and rhinoceros-horn belts; I know this well and could surely retrieve them if sent."
translations.idiomatic: That year, once Huai West was pacified, Yuanqing memorialized, "The region holds great treasure and rhinoceros-horn belts. I know where they are and could recover them if dispatched."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕本討賊，為人除害，今賊平人安，則我求之得矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I undertook this campaign to remove a scourge from the people. Now that the rebels are crushed and the people are at peace, I have already gained what I sought.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "I raised this army to rid the people of a scourge. With the rebels gone and the realm at peace, I have already won what I sought.

sentences.zh: 寶貨犀帶，非所求也，勿復此言。」

translations.literal: Valuables and rhinoceros-horn belts are not what I seek—do not speak of this again."
translations.idiomatic: Treasure and rhinoceros-horn belts were never my aim. Do not raise this again."

sentences.zh: 是月，詔授左金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: That month an edict appointed him general of the Left Jinwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: That month he was appointed general of the Left Jinwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改汾州刺史，復征為左金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Prefect of Fenzhou, then recalled again as general of the Left Jinwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as Prefect of Fenzhou, then recalled once more as general of the Left Jinwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，易置鎮、魏守臣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing the garrison commanders of Zhen and Wei were replaced.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Changqing the commanders of the Zhen and Wei garrisons were reshuffled.

sentences.zh: 元卿詣宰相深陳利害，並具表其事。

translations.literal: Yuanqing went to the chief ministers and explained the advantages and dangers in depth, and also submitted a detailed memorial on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing went to the chief ministers and laid out the risks and benefits at length, backing his argument with a full memorial.

sentences.zh: 後穆宗感悟，賜白玉帶，旋授檢校左散騎常侍、涇州刺史、涇原渭節度觀察等使，兼充四鎮北庭行軍。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Muzong was moved to understanding; he granted Yuanqing a white jade belt and soon appointed him acting Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, Prefect of Jingzhou, military commissioner and surveillance commissioner of Jing-Yuan-Wei, and concurrently commander of the Four Garrisons Northern Court campaign army.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Muzong took his counsel to heart, granted him a white jade belt, and soon made him acting Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, Prefect of Jingzhou, military commissioner and surveillance commissioner of Jing-Yuan-Wei, and commander of the Four Garrisons Northern Court campaign force.

sentences.zh: 元卿乃奏置屯田五千頃，每屯築墻高數仞，鍵閉牢密，卒然寇至，盡可保守。

translations.literal: Yuanqing then memorialized to establish five thousand qing of garrison farms; at each colony walls several ren high were built, locked and sealed tight and secure, so that if raiders suddenly arrived everything could still be defended.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing then memorialized the throne to establish five thousand qing of military colony fields. At each settlement he had walls built several ren high, locked and sealed so they were secure; if raiders suddenly struck, every site could still be held.

sentences.zh: 加檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 營田成，復加使號。

translations.literal: When the garrison farms were completed, he received another honorific commissioner title.
translations.idiomatic: Once the colony farms were finished, he was given an additional commissioner title.

sentences.zh: 居六年，涇人論奏，為立德政碑，移授懷州刺史，充河陽三城節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: After six years in office, the people of Jing submitted a collective petition and had a monument to his virtuous governance erected; he was transferred to prefect of Huai and appointed military commissioner and inspector of Heyang's three cities and related posts.
translations.idiomatic: After six years in office, the people of Jing submitted a joint petition and erected a monument to his virtuous rule. He was transferred to prefect of Huai and made military commissioner and inspector of the Heyang Three Cities and related posts.

sentences.zh: 太和五年，就加檢校司空，進階光祿大夫，以其營田納粟二十萬石，以裨經費故也。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe he was further promoted to Acting Sikong and advanced to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, because his garrison farms had delivered two hundred thousand shi of grain to supplement state expenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taihe he was further promoted to Acting Sikong and to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, in recognition of the two hundred thousand shi of grain his colony farms had delivered to help meet state expenses.

sentences.zh: 是歲，改授汴宋亳觀察等使。

translations.literal: That year he was reassigned as inspector of Bian, Song, Bo and related posts.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was reassigned as inspector of Bian, Song, Bo, and related posts.

sentences.zh: 凡所廢置，皆有弘益，詔並從之。

translations.literal: Everything he had abolished or established was greatly beneficial; edicts approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: Every measure he abolished or instituted proved broadly beneficial, and the throne approved them all.

sentences.zh: 年七十，寢疾，歸洛陽，詔授太子太保。

translations.literal: At age seventy he fell ill in bed, returned to Luoyang, and was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent by edict.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy he took to his bed with illness, returned to Luoyang, and was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 是歲八月卒，廢朝三日，贈司徒。

translations.literal: He died in the eighth month that year; court mourning was suspended for three days, and he was posthumously awarded the title of Situ.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of that year. Court was suspended for three days of mourning, and he was posthumously enfeoffed as Situ.

sentences.zh: 元卿始以毀家效順，累授方鎮。

translations.literal: Yuanqing had initially won favor by ruining his own family to show loyalty, and was repeatedly appointed to regional commands.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing had first won the court's trust by sacrificing his own household to prove his loyalty, and was repeatedly given regional commands.

sentences.zh: 然性險巧，所至好聚斂，善結交，涇人得情，亦由此也。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was crafty and scheming; wherever he went he loved to accumulate wealth and was skilled at cultivating connections. That was also why he won the affection of the people of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was by nature cunning and scheming, loved to amass wealth wherever he served, and was adept at cultivating allies. That was also how he won the goodwill of the people of Jing.

sentences.zh: 子延宗，開成中為磁州刺史，坐謀逐河陽節度使以自立，為其黨所告，臺司推鞫得實，誅之。

translations.literal: His son Yanzong served as prefect of Ci in the Kaicheng era; he was charged with plotting to drive out the Heyang military commissioner so he could set himself up independently, was reported by his own faction, the censorate investigated and confirmed the facts, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanzong served as prefect of Ci during the Kaicheng era. He was found guilty of plotting to expel the Heyang military commissioner and set himself up in power; his own associates reported him, the censorate investigated and confirmed the charge, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 劉悟，正臣之孫也。

translations.literal: Liu Wu—Liu Wu was the grandson of Zhengchen.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wu was the grandson of Liu Zhengchen.

sentences.zh: 正臣本名客奴。

translations.literal: Zhengchen's original name was Kernu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengchen's original name had been Kernu.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，祿山叛，平盧軍節度使柳知晦受賊偽署。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era Lushan rebelled; Liu Zhihui, military commissioner of the Pinglu army, accepted a fraudulent appointment from the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Tianbao era, when An Lushan rebelled, Liu Zhihui, military commissioner of the Pinglu army, accepted a bogus commission from the rebels.

sentences.zh: 客奴時職居牙門，襲殺知晦，馳章以聞。

translations.literal: Kernu at the time held a post in the headquarters guard; he launched a surprise attack and killed Zhihui, then dispatched a memorial at speed to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Kernu then held a post in the headquarters guard. He launched a surprise attack, killed Zhihui, and sent an urgent memorial to report what he had done.

sentences.zh: 授平盧軍節度使，賜名正臣。

translations.literal: He was appointed military commissioner of the Pinglu army and granted the name Zhengchen.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military commissioner of the Pinglu army and given the name Zhengchen.

sentences.zh: 悟少有勇力。

translations.literal: Wu in his youth possessed courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Wu was known for courage and physical strength.

sentences.zh: 叔逸準為汴帥，積緡錢數百萬於洛中；

translations.literal: His uncle Yizhun was military commissioner of Bian and had accumulated several million strings of cash in Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Yizhun was military commissioner of Bian and had stored several million strings of cash in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 悟輒破扃鐍，悉盜用之。

translations.literal: Wu broke the locks and stole the whole sum for his own use.
translations.idiomatic: Wu broke the locks and stole the entire sum for himself.

sentences.zh: 既而懼，亡歸李師古。

translations.literal: Then, afraid, he fled and returned to Li Shigu.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the consequences, he fled and took refuge with Li Shigu.

sentences.zh: 始亦未甚知，後因擊球馳突，沖師古馬仆，師古怒，將斬之。

translations.literal: At first Shigu did not pay him much notice; later, while playing cavalry polo Wu charged recklessly, knocked Shigu's horse down, and Shigu in anger was about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shigu paid him little heed. Later, during a game of mounted polo, Wu charged recklessly and knocked Shigu from his horse. Shigu flew into a rage and was about to have him executed.

sentences.zh: 悟猛以氣語押觸師古，師古奇而免之。

translations.literal: Wu boldly confronted Shigu with fierce words; Shigu thought him remarkable and spared him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu answered back with fierce, defiant words. Shigu found him remarkable and spared his life.

sentences.zh: 因令管壯士，將後軍，累署衙門右職，奏授淄青節度都知兵馬使、兼監察御史。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was put in charge of stalwart fighters and commanded the rear guard; he successively held senior posts in headquarters and was memorialized for appointment as overall commander of Ziqing's forces and concurrent Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was then put in charge of elite troops and given command of the rear guard. He rose through senior headquarters posts and was memorialized for appointment as overall commander of the Ziqing forces and concurrent Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 元和末，憲宗既平淮西，下詔誅師道。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanhe era, after Xianzong had pacified Huai-Xi, an edict was issued condemning Shidao.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanhe era, once Xianzong had pacified Huai-Xi, the court issued an edict calling for Li Shidao's execution.

sentences.zh: 遣悟將兵拒魏博軍，而數促悟戰。

translations.literal: Wu was sent to lead troops against the Weibo army and was repeatedly pressed to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was ordered to lead troops against the Weibo army, and was repeatedly urged to engage.

sentences.zh: 悟未及進，馳使召之。

translations.literal: Before Wu could advance, a fast messenger was sent to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wu could move forward, an urgent messenger was dispatched to summon him.

sentences.zh: 悟度使來必殺己，乃偽疾不出，令都虞候往迎之。

translations.literal: Wu judged that when the envoy arrived he would surely be killed; he therefore feigned illness and did not appear, sending the chief adjutant to meet the messenger instead.
translations.idiomatic: Wu concluded that the envoy had come to kill him. He feigned illness and refused to appear, sending his chief adjutant to meet the messenger in his place.

sentences.zh: 使者亦果以誠告其人，雲「奉命殺悟以代悟」。

translations.literal: The envoy indeed confided the truth to that man, saying, "I have orders to kill Wu and take his place."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy did in fact confide the truth to the adjutant, saying, "I have orders to kill Wu and replace him."

sentences.zh: 都虞候即時先還，悟劾之得其實，乃召諸將與謀曰：「魏博田弘正兵強，出戰必敗，不出則死。

translations.literal: The chief adjutant returned at once; Wu investigated and confirmed the facts, then summoned the generals to deliberate, saying, "Tian Hongzheng of Weibo has strong troops. If we go out to fight we are sure to lose; if we do not go out we still die.
translations.idiomatic: The chief adjutant returned immediately. Wu investigated, confirmed the plot, and summoned his generals to counsel them: "Tian Hongzheng of Weibo commands strong troops. If we take the field we are sure to be defeated; if we refuse, we die all the same.

sentences.zh: 今天子所誅者，司空一人而已，悟與公等皆為所驅迫，使就其死。

translations.literal: Today the Son of Heaven seeks to execute only the Chief Minister alone; Wu and all of you are being driven and forced to meet death with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven means to punish the Chief Minister alone. Wu and all of you are being driven to die with him.

sentences.zh: 何如殺其來使，整戈以取鄆，立大功，轉危亡為富貴耶！」

translations.literal: Why not kill the incoming envoy, ready our weapons, seize Yun, perform a great deed, and turn peril and destruction into wealth and honor!"
translations.idiomatic: Why not kill this envoy, take up our arms, seize Yun, win a great victory, and turn disaster into fortune and honor?"

sentences.zh: 眾咸曰：「善，唯都將所命！」

translations.literal: All said, "Good—we will obey whatever the commander orders!"
translations.idiomatic: They all answered, "Well said—we will do whatever the commander orders!"

sentences.zh: 悟於是立斬其使，以兵取鄆，圍其內城，兼以火攻其門。

translations.literal: Wu thereupon immediately executed the envoy, took troops to seize Yun, besieged the inner city, and also attacked the gates with fire.
translations.idiomatic: Wu immediately executed the envoy, marched on Yun with his troops, besieged the inner city, and set fire to the gates.

sentences.zh: 不數刻，擒師道並男二人，並斬其首以獻。

translations.literal: Within a few quarter-hours he captured Shidao along with two sons, beheaded all of them, and presented their heads.
translations.idiomatic: Within scarcely a quarter-hour he captured Shidao and two of his sons, beheaded all three, and sent their heads to the court.

sentences.zh: 擢拜悟檢校工部尚書、兼御史大夫、義成軍節度使，封彭城郡王，仍賜實封五百戶，錢二萬貫，莊、宅各一區。

translations.literal: Wu was promoted to Acting Minister of Works, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and military commissioner of Yicheng; enfeoffed as Prince of Pengcheng Commandery; and furthermore granted five hundred taxable households, twenty thousand strings of cash, and one estate and one residence.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was promoted to Acting Minister of Works and Censor-in-Chief, and made military commissioner of Yicheng. He was enfeoffed as Prince of Pengcheng Commandery and granted five hundred taxable households, twenty thousand strings of cash, and both an estate and a residence.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月入覲，又加檢校兵部尚書，余如故。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year he came to audience; he was further given Acting Minister of War, the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year he came to court. He was further appointed Acting Minister of War; his other titles remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，以恩例遷檢校尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: When Muzong acceded, by grace precedent he was transferred to Acting Vice Director of the Right Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong took the throne, Wu was transferred by grace precedent to Acting Vice Director of the Right Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 是歲十月，移鎮澤潞，旋以本官兼平章事。

translations.literal: That October he was shifted to command Ze-Lu; soon afterward he held his existing rank concurrently as Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: That October he was transferred to command Ze-Lu, and soon afterward was given his existing rank concurrently with the title of Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年，幽州大將硃克融叛，囚其帥張弘靖，朝廷求名將以鎮漁陽。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing, Zhu Kerong, a major general of Youzhou, rebelled and imprisoned his commander Zhang Hongjing; the court sought a famous general to secure Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changqing, Zhu Kerong, a senior general of Youzhou, rebelled and imprisoned his commander Zhang Hongjing. The court looked for a renowned general to secure Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 乃加悟檢校司空、平章事，充盧龍軍節度使。

translations.literal: Wu was given Acting Sikong, Grand Councilor, and appointed military commissioner of Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was promoted to Acting Sikong and Grand Councilor and appointed military commissioner of Lulong.

sentences.zh: 悟以幽州方亂，未克進討，請授之節鉞，徐圖之。

translations.literal: Because Youzhou was still in turmoil and he could not yet advance to suppress it, Wu asked to be granted the command flag and seal and plan slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou was still in chaos and he could not yet march to suppress the rebellion, so Wu asked to be granted the command seal and take his time planning the campaign.

sentences.zh: 乃復以悟為澤潞節度，拜檢校司徒，兼太子太傅，依前平章事。

translations.literal: He was then returned to command Ze-Lu, appointed Acting Situ, Concurrent Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and continued as before as Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was then returned to command Ze-Lu, appointed Acting Situ and Concurrent Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and retained his post as Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 時監軍劉承偕頗恃恩權，常對眾辱悟；

translations.literal: At the time army supervisor Liu Chengjie relied heavily on imperial favor and authority; he often humiliated Wu before the assembled troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the army supervisor Liu Chengjie leaned heavily on imperial favor and often humiliated Wu in front of the assembled troops.

sentences.zh: 又縱其下亂法，悟不能平。

translations.literal: He also let his subordinates violate regulations with impunity; Wu could not remain calm about it.
translations.idiomatic: He also allowed his men to break regulations with impunity, and Wu could not endure it.

sentences.zh: 異日有中使至，承偕宴之，請悟，悟欲往。

translations.literal: One day when an imperial envoy arrived, Chengjie entertained him and invited Wu; Wu was about to go.
translations.idiomatic: One day an imperial envoy arrived. Chengjie entertained him and invited Wu to join; Wu was about to go.

sentences.zh: 左右皆曰：「往則必為其困辱矣！」

translations.literal: Those around him all said, "If you go you will surely be trapped and humiliated!"
translations.idiomatic: Those around him said, "If you go, he is sure to trap and humiliate you!"

sentences.zh: 軍眾因亂，悟不止之。

translations.literal: The troops then fell into disorder, and Wu did not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: The troops erupted in disorder, and Wu did not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 乃擒承偕至牙門，殺其二仆，欲並害承偕，悟救之獲免。

translations.literal: They seized Chengjie and brought him to headquarters, killed two of his attendants, and were about to kill Chengjie as well; Wu rescued him and he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Chengjie and dragged him to headquarters, killed two of his attendants, and were about to kill Chengjie himself. Wu intervened and saved him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不獲已，貶承偕。

translations.literal: The court, unable to do otherwise, demoted Chengjie.
translations.idiomatic: The court, having no other choice, demoted Chengjie.

sentences.zh: 自是悟頗縱恣，欲效河朔三鎮。

translations.literal: From then on Wu grew quite unrestrained and wished to emulate the three Hebei circuits.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Wu grew increasingly unrestrained and sought to imitate the three Hebei circuits.

sentences.zh: 朝廷失意不逞之徒，多投寄潞州以求援。

translations.literal: Many who had lost favor at court and could not get their way took refuge in Lu Prefecture seeking support.
translations.idiomatic: Many men who had fallen from favor at court and could not have their way took refuge in Lu Prefecture seeking his backing.

sentences.zh: 往往奏章論事，辭旨不遜。

translations.literal: They often submitted memorials on affairs with language that was insubordinate.
translations.idiomatic: They often submitted memorials on state affairs in language that was openly insubordinate.

sentences.zh: 寶歷元年九月病卒，贈太尉。

translations.literal: He died of illness in the ninth month of the first year of Baoli and was posthumously awarded Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in the ninth month of the first year of Baoli and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 遺表請以其子從諫繼纘戎事。

translations.literal: In his final memorial he requested that his son Congjian succeed to military command.
translations.idiomatic: In his deathbed memorial he asked that his son Congjian succeed to command of the army.

sentences.zh: 敬宗下大臣議。

translations.literal: Emperor Jingzong submitted the matter to his ministers for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong referred the request to his ministers for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 僕射李絳以澤潞內地，與三鎮事理不同，不可許。

translations.literal: Vice Director Li Jiang held that Ze-Lu was interior territory and differed in principle from the three circuits; it could not be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Li Jiang argued that Ze-Lu lay in the interior and was fundamentally unlike the three circuits, and that the request could not be granted.

sentences.zh: 宰相李逢吉、中尉王守澄受其賂，曲為奏請。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Li Fengji and the Chief Palace Steward Wang Shoucheng accepted bribes from them and contrived memorials on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Fengji and Chief Palace Steward Wang Shoucheng accepted bribes from the family and maneuvered a memorial in their favor.

sentences.zh: 從諫自將作監主簿，起復雲麾將軍，守金吾衛大將軍同正、檢校左散騎常侍、兼御史大夫，充昭義節度副大使，知節度觀察等留後。

translations.literal: Congjian rose from Master Recorder in the Directorate for Palace Buildings; recalled from mourning as General of the Cloud-Banner Guard; appointed Acting Left Regular Attendant; concurrent Censor-in-Chief; deputy military commissioner of Zhaoyi; and acting inspector of the circuit and related duties.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian was recalled from mourning from his post as Master Recorder in the Directorate for Palace Buildings, appointed General of the Cloud-Banner Guard, Acting Left Regular Attendant, and Censor-in-Chief, and made deputy military commissioner of Zhaoyi with acting authority over the circuit and related duties.

sentences.zh: 二年，加金吾上將軍、檢校工部尚書，充昭義節度等使。

translations.literal: In the second year he was given Senior General of the Golden Guard, Acting Minister of Works, and full military commissioner of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed Senior General of the Golden Guard, Acting Minister of Works, and full military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，進檢校司空。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong acceded, he was advanced to Acting Sikong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, Congjian was promoted to Acting Sikong.

sentences.zh: 六年十二月入覲。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the sixth year he came to audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the sixth year he came to court.

sentences.zh: 七年春歸籓，加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year he returned to his post and was given Concurrent Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year he returned to his command and was made Concurrent Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 九年，李訓事敗，宰相王涯等四人被禍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Li Xun affair failed; Grand Councilor Wang Ya and three others met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Li Xun plot failed, and Grand Councilor Wang Ya and three others were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 時涯兼掌邦計，雖不與李訓同謀，然不自異於其間，既死非其罪。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Ya also oversaw state finance; though he had not conspired with Li Xun, he had not kept himself apart from the affair, and his death was not deserved.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya was then also in charge of state finance. Though he had not plotted with Li Xun, he had not kept himself apart from the affair, and his execution was undeserved.

sentences.zh: 從諫素德涯之私恩，心頗不平，四上章請涯等罪名，仇士良輩深憚之。

translations.literal: Congjian had long owed Wang Ya a personal debt of gratitude and was quite unsettled in mind; four times he submitted memorials asking what crimes Wang Ya and the others had committed; Qiu Shiliang and his faction deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian had long felt a personal debt to Wang Ya and was deeply troubled by the case. Four times he memorialized asking what crimes Wang Ya and the others had committed. Qiu Shiliang and his faction feared him greatly.

sentences.zh: 是時中官頗橫，天子不能制。

translations.literal: At that time eunuch officials were quite overbearing and the emperor could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the eunuch officials were rampant, and the emperor could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 朝臣日憂陷族，賴從諫論列，而鄭覃、李石方能粗秉朝政。

translations.literal: Court officials daily feared the extermination of their clans; they relied on Congjian's forthright memorials, and only then could Zheng Tan and Li Shi roughly hold the reins of court governance.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials lived in daily fear that their entire clans would be wiped out. They depended on Congjian's outspoken memorials, and only then could Zheng Tan and Li Shi roughly hold the reins of government.

sentences.zh: 先是，有蕭洪者，詐稱太后弟，因仇士良保任，許之厚賂。

translations.literal: Previously there had been a Xiao Hong who falsely claimed to be the empress dowager's younger brother; through Qiu Shiliang's sponsorship he promised rich bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier there had been a man named Xiao Hong who falsely claimed to be the empress dowager's younger brother. With Qiu Shiliang's backing he promised lavish bribes.

sentences.zh: 及洪累授方鎮，納賂不滿士良之誌，士良怒，遣人上書論洪非太后之親，又以蕭本者為太后弟。

translations.literal: When Hong was repeatedly appointed to regional commands, the bribes he paid did not satisfy Shiliang's desires; Shiliang in anger sent someone to submit a memorial arguing that Hong was not the empress dowager's kinsman, and asserted that Xiao Ben was the empress dowager's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: After Hong was repeatedly given regional commands, the bribes he paid failed to satisfy Shiliang. Shiliang in anger had someone submit a memorial claiming Hong was not the empress dowager's kinsman, and declared that Xiao Ben was her true younger brother.

sentences.zh: 從諫深知內宮之故，乃自潞府飛章論之曰：「臣聞造偽以亂真者，匹夫知之尚不可，況天下皆知乎？

translations.literal: Congjian knew well the inner-palace background, and therefore from Lu sent an urgent memorial arguing: "Your subject has heard that to manufacture falsehood to confound truth—even if a common man knows of it that cannot be tolerated, how much less when all under Heaven knows?
translations.idiomatic: Congjian understood the inner-palace intrigue behind the affair and sent an urgent memorial from Lu, writing: "I have heard that to manufacture falsehood and confound the truth cannot be tolerated even when only a common man knows of it—how much less when all the realm knows?

sentences.zh: 執疏以為親者，在匹夫之家尚不可，況處大國之朝乎？

translations.literal: To clutch a document and declare someone a relative—even in a commoner's household that cannot be allowed, how much less in the court of a great state?
translations.idiomatic: To clutch a written claim and declare someone a kinsman cannot be allowed even in a commoner's household—how much less in the court of a great empire?

sentences.zh: 臣受國恩深，奉公心切，知有此失，安敢不言！

translations.literal: Your subject has received deep grace from the state and serves the public with urgent devotion; knowing of this wrong, how could I dare not speak!
translations.idiomatic: I have received deep grace from the state and serve the public with all my heart. Knowing of this wrong, how could I dare remain silent?

sentences.zh: 伏唯皇帝陛下仁及萬方，孝敦九族，而推心無黨，唯理是求。

translations.literal: Bow before Your Majesty's benevolence reaching all regions, filial piety extending through the nine clans, an open heart without faction, seeking only what is right.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's benevolence reaches every quarter, your filial piety embraces the nine clans, your heart is open and without faction, and you seek only what is right.

sentences.zh: 微臣所以不避直言，切論深事。

translations.literal: That is why this lowly subject does not avoid blunt speech and urgently addresses so grave a matter.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I do not shrink from blunt speech on so grave a matter.

sentences.zh: 伏見金吾將軍蕭本，稱是太后親弟，受此官榮。

translations.literal: I observe that General of the Golden Guard Xiao Ben claims to be the empress dowager's own younger brother and has received this rank and honor.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that General of the Golden Guard Xiao Ben claims to be the empress dowager's own younger brother and has been granted rank and honor on that basis.

sentences.zh: 今喧然國都，迨聞籓府，自上及下，異口同音，皆言蕭弘是真，蕭本是偽。

translations.literal: Now there is uproar in the capital, and the news has reached the frontier posts; from high to low, with one voice all say that Xiao Hong is genuine and Xiao Ben is false.
translations.idiomatic: Now the capital is in an uproar, and the news has spread to the frontier posts. From high to low, all say with one voice that Xiao Hong is genuine and Xiao Ben is a fraud.

sentences.zh: 臣傍聽眾論，遍察群情，鹹思發明，以正名分。

translations.literal: Your subject has listened to public talk on every side and surveyed the feelings of the group; all wish this clarified to set names and ranks aright.
translations.idiomatic: I have listened to public opinion on every side and weighed the mood of the court. All wish this matter clarified so that names and ranks may be set aright.

sentences.zh: 今年二月，其蕭弘投臣當道，求臣上聞，自言：比者福建觀察使唐扶及監軍劉行立具審根源，已曾論奏。

translations.literal: This year in the second month that Xiao Hong came before me on the road and asked me to report upward; he said that recently Fujian observation commissioner Tang Fu and army supervisor Liu Xingli had fully examined the origins and had already memorialized on it.
translations.idiomatic: This year, in the second month, Xiao Hong came to me on the road and asked me to report his case to the throne. He said that Fujian observation commissioner Tang Fu and army supervisor Liu Xingli had already fully investigated the matter and submitted a memorial on it.

sentences.zh: 其時屬蕭本得為外戚，來自左軍，臺司既不敢研窮，聖意遂勒還鄉里。

translations.literal: At that time, since Xiao Ben had become an imperial relative through the empress dowager and came from the Left Army, the censorial offices dared not investigate thoroughly, and the imperial will ordered Hong to return to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiao Ben had become an imperial in-law through the empress dowager and enjoyed backing from the Left Army. The censorial offices dared not pursue the matter, and the throne ordered Xiao Hong sent back to his home district.

sentences.zh: 自茲議論，轉益沸騰。

translations.literal: Since then debate has grown ever more heated.
translations.idiomatic: Since then public debate has grown ever fiercer.

sentences.zh: 臣亦令潛問左軍，榷論大體，而士良推至公之道，發不黨之言。

translations.literal: Your subject also had inquiries made secretly of the Left Army and weighed the larger issue; Shiliang spoke in favor of utmost fairness and issued words of no partiality.
translations.idiomatic: I also made discreet inquiries of the Left Army and weighed the larger issue. Shiliang spoke of utmost fairness and declared himself free of partiality.

sentences.zh: 蓋蕭本自度孤危，妄有憑恃。

translations.literal: It appears Xiao Ben judged himself isolated and endangered, and presumptuously sought something to lean on.
translations.idiomatic: It appears Xiao Ben saw himself isolated and imperiled, and presumptuously sought something to lean on.

sentences.zh: 伏以名居國舅，位列朝班，而真偽不分，中外所恥。

translations.literal: One bearing the name of imperial uncle-in-law, holding rank in the court assembly, yet with truth and falsehood undistinguished—this shames court and frontier alike.
translations.idiomatic: A man who bears the title of imperial uncle-in-law and holds rank in the court assembly, yet with truth and falsehood left undistinguished—this shames both court and frontier alike.

sentences.zh: 切慮皇太后受此罔惑，已有恩情，若含垢於一時，終取笑於千古。

translations.literal: I deeply fear the empress dowager has been deceived by this and has already formed affectionate feeling; if we tolerate this stain for a moment, we will invite ridicule for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: I deeply fear the empress dowager has been misled and has already formed an affectionate bond with the impostor. If we tolerate this stain even for a moment, we will invite ridicule for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 伏乞追蕭弘赴闕，與蕭本對推，細詰根源，必辨真偽。」

translations.literal: I beg that Xiao Hong be summoned to the capital to confront and examine matters with Xiao Ben, that the origins be questioned in detail, and truth and falsehood decisively distinguished."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Xiao Hong be summoned to the capital to confront Xiao Ben, that the origins be examined in detail, and truth and falsehood decisively distinguished."

sentences.zh: 詔令三司使推按。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Three Offices commissioners to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Three Offices commissioners to investigate the case.

sentences.zh: 帝以二蕭雖詐，托名太后之宗，不欲誅之，俱流嶺表。

translations.literal: The emperor, because both Xiaos though fraudulent invoked the empress dowager's clan, did not wish to execute them; both were banished beyond the Ling region.
translations.idiomatic: Because both impostors had invoked the empress dowager's clan, the emperor did not wish to execute them. Both were banished to the far south beyond the Ling region.

sentences.zh: 從諫進位檢校司徒。

translations.literal: Congjian advanced to Acting Situ.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian was promoted to Acting Situ.

sentences.zh: 會昌三年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Huichang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Huichang.

sentences.zh: 大將郭誼等匿喪，用其侄稹權領軍務。

translations.literal: Major generals including Guo Yi concealed the death and used his nephew Zhen to take military affairs in hand.
translations.idiomatic: Senior generals including Guo Yi concealed his death and put his nephew Zhen in charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 時宰相李德裕用事，素惡從諫之奸回，奏請劉稹護喪歸洛，以聽朝旨。

translations.literal: At the time Chief Minister Li Deyu held power and had long hated Congjian's treacherous ways; he memorialized that Liu Zhen should escort the coffin back to Luoyang and await the court's command.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Deyu was then in power and had long despised Congjian's duplicity. He memorialized that Liu Zhen should escort the coffin back to Luoyang and await the court's orders.

sentences.zh: 稹竟叛。

translations.literal: Zhen ultimately rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen rebelled in the end.

sentences.zh: 德裕用中丞李回奉使河朔，說令三鎮加兵討稹；

translations.literal: Deyu employed Censor-in-Chief Li Hui on a mission to the Hebei region to persuade the three circuits to add troops to attack Zhen;
translations.idiomatic: Deyu sent Censor-in-Chief Li Hui as envoy to the Hebei region to persuade the three circuits to commit additional troops against Zhen.

sentences.zh: 乃削奪稹官，命徐許滑孟魏鎮幽并八鎮之師，四面進攻。

translations.literal: Zhen's offices were then stripped; forces of the eight circuits—Xuzhou, Xu Prefecture, Huazhou, Mengzhou, Weibo, Zhenzhou, Youzhou, and Bingzhou—were ordered to attack from all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's offices were then stripped. Armies from Xuzhou, Xu Prefecture, Huazhou, Mengzhou, Weibo, Zhenzhou, Youzhou, and Bingzhou were ordered to attack from every direction.

sentences.zh: 四年，郭誼斬稹，傳首京師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Guo Yi executed Zhen and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Guo Yi executed Zhen and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 從諫妻裴氏。

translations.literal: Congjian's wife was Lady Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian's wife was Lady Pei.

sentences.zh: 初，稹拒命，裴氏召集大將妻同宴，以酒為壽，泣下不能已。

translations.literal: When Zhen first defied orders, Lady Pei gathered the generals' wives for a banquet together, offered wine in celebration, and wept without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen first defied the court's orders, Lady Pei gathered the generals' wives for a banquet, raised a cup in toast, and wept without stopping.

sentences.zh: 諸婦請命，裴曰：「新婦各與汝夫文字，勿忘先相公之拔擢，莫效李丕背恩，走投國家。

translations.literal: The wives asked what was wrong; Lady Pei said, "Each of you new brides write letters to your husbands: do not forget how the late lord elevated you; do not imitate Li Pi, who betrayed his grace and fled to the state's enemies.
translations.idiomatic: The wives asked what troubled her. Lady Pei said, "Each of you new brides write to your husbands: do not forget how the late lord raised you up, and do not follow Li Pi's example by betraying his grace and turning against the state.

sentences.zh: 子母為托，故悲不能已也。」

translations.literal: It is my son I entrust to you—that is why my grief will not stop."
translations.idiomatic: It is my son I entrust to you—that is why I cannot stop weeping."

sentences.zh: 諸婦亦泣下，故潞將叛誌益堅。

translations.literal: The other wives also wept, and thus the resolve of the Lu generals to rebel grew firmer still.
translations.idiomatic: The other wives wept as well, and the Lu commanders' determination to rebel hardened all the more.

sentences.zh: 稹死，裴亦以此極刑。

translations.literal: When Zhen died, Pei also received the extreme penalty for this.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhen was executed, Lady Pei was put to death by the same extreme penalty.

sentences.zh: 稹族屬昆仲九人，皆誅。

translations.literal: Nine male relatives of Zhen's clan were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Nine male members of Zhen's clan were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 劉沔，許州牙將也。

translations.literal: Liu Mian—Liu Mian was a yamen guard officer of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian was a guard officer in the Xuzhou military yamen.

sentences.zh: 少事李光顏為帳中親將。

translations.literal: In youth he served Li Guangyan as an intimate general in the commander's personal staff.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served Li Guangyan as a trusted general on his personal staff.

sentences.zh: 元和末，光顏討吳元濟，常用沔為前鋒。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanhe era, when Guangyan campaigned against Wu Yuanji, he often used Mian as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanhe reign, when Guangyan marched against Wu Yuanji, he regularly sent Mian ahead as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 蔡將有董重質者，守洄曲，其部下乘騾即戰，號「騾子軍」，最為勁悍，官軍常警備之。

translations.literal: Among the Cai generals was Dong Chongzhi, who held Huaiqu; his subordinates fought mounted on mules and were called the "Mule Army"—they were the fiercest and most formidable, and government troops were always on guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: One of the Cai generals, Dong Chongzhi, held Huaiqu. His men fought from muleback and were known as the "Mule Army"—the toughest force in the field, and one the imperial armies always treated with caution.

sentences.zh: 沔驍銳善騎射，每與騾軍接戰，必冒刃陷堅，俘馘而還，故忠武一軍，破賊第一。

translations.literal: Mian was bold and sharp, skilled in mounted archery; whenever he clashed with the Mule Army he braved blades and broke through their line, taking captives and heads before returning. Thus within the Zhongwu army he ranked first in defeating the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was fierce, quick, and a superb mounted archer. In every clash with the Mule Army he charged through the blades, broke the enemy line, and came back with prisoners and severed heads. Among the Zhongwu forces he stood first in breaking the rebels.

sentences.zh: 淮、蔡平，隨光顏入朝。

translations.literal: When Huai and Cai were pacified, he followed Guangyan to court.
translations.idiomatic: After Huai and Cai were pacified, he accompanied Guangyan to the capital.

sentences.zh: 憲宗留宿衛，歷三將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong kept him in the palace guard, and he rose through three generalships.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong retained him in the palace guard, where he rose through three general's ranks.

sentences.zh: 歷鹽州刺史、天德軍防禦使，在西北邊累立奇效。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Yanzhou and defense commissioner of the Tiande army, and on the northwest frontier won repeated outstanding achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Yanzhou and defense commissioner of the Tiande army, winning one outstanding victory after another on the northwest frontier.

sentences.zh: 太和末，河西党項羌叛。

translations.literal: At the end of the Taihe era the Tangut Qiang of Hexi rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Taihe reign the Tangut Qiang of Hexi rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 沔以天德之師屢誅其酋渠，移授振武節度使，檢校右散騎常侍、單於大都護。

translations.literal: Mian repeatedly killed their chieftains with the Tiande forces, and was transferred to be military commissioner of Zhenwu, acting Right Regular Grand Master of the Palace Retinue, and Grand Protector of Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: With the Tiande army Mian repeatedly killed their chieftains. He was then transferred to military commissioner of Zhenwu, with the acting titles of Right Regular Grand Master of the Palace Retinue and Grand Protector of Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 開成中，党項雜虜大擾河西。

translations.literal: In the Kaicheng era the Tangut and various other tribes made great disturbances in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaicheng reign the Tangut and other frontier tribes threw Hexi into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 沔率吐渾、契苾、沙陁三部落等諸族萬人、馬三千騎，徑至銀、夏討襲，大破之。

translations.literal: Mian led more than ten thousand men from the Tuquhun, Qibi, and Shatuo tribes and other clans, with three thousand cavalry, straight to Yin and Xia to attack and raid, and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Mian led ten thousand men from the Tuquhun, Qibi, Shatuo, and other allied tribes, with three thousand horsemen, straight into Yin and Xia to strike and raid, and broke them completely.

sentences.zh: 俘獲萬計，告捷而還。

translations.literal: Captives numbered in the tens of thousands; he reported victory and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Captives ran into the tens of thousands. He reported victory and returned.

sentences.zh: 以功加檢校戶部尚書。

translations.literal: For this achievement he was further appointed acting Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was further appointed acting Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，回紇部饑，烏介可汗奉太和公主至漢南求食。

translations.literal: At the start of the Huichang era the Uyghur tribes suffered famine, and Khagan Wujie led Princess Taihe south of the Han frontier to seek food.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Huichang reign famine struck the Uyghur tribes, and Khagan Wujie led Princess Taihe south of the frontier to seek provisions.

sentences.zh: 過杷頭峰，犯雲、朔、北川。

translations.literal: Passing Batou Peak, he violated Yun, Shuo, and Beichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Batou Peak, he raided Yun, Shuo, and Beichuan.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以太原重地，控扼諸戎，乃移沔河東節度使、檢校尚書左僕射、太原尹、北京留守。

translations.literal: The court, considering Taiyuan a vital region for controlling the frontier peoples, transferred Mian to be Hedong military commissioner, acting Left Vice Minister of Works, Taiyuan magistrate, and Northern Capital garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Because Taiyuan was a vital choke point for the frontier peoples, the court transferred Mian to Hedong military commissioner, with the acting titles of Left Vice Minister of Works, Taiyuan magistrate, and Northern Capital garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 詔與幽州張仲武協力招撫回鶻，竟破虜寇，迎公主還宮。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to work with Zhang Zhongwu of Youzhou to pacify the Uyghurs by conciliation; in the end they broke the barbarian raiders and escorted the princess back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to join Zhang Zhongwu of Youzhou in winning the Uyghurs over by conciliation. In the end they shattered the raiders and escorted the princess back to court.

sentences.zh: 以功進位檢校司空，尋改滑州刺史、義成軍節度使。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to acting Grand Master of Works, and soon after made prefect of Huazhou and military commissioner of the Yicheng army.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to acting Grand Master of Works, and soon after was made prefect of Huazhou and military commissioner of the Yicheng army.

sentences.zh: 四年，潞帥劉從諫卒，子稹匿喪，擅主留務，要求旌鉞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Liu Congjian, military commissioner of Lu, died; his son Zhen concealed the death and on his own authority took charge of local affairs, demanding the commissioner's staff and ceremonial axe.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Liu Congjian, military commissioner of Lu, died. His son Zhen concealed the death, seized control of local affairs on his own authority, and demanded the commissioner's staff and ceremonial axe.

sentences.zh: 武宗怒，命忠武節度使王宰、徐州節度李彥佐等，充潞府西南面招撫使。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong was enraged and ordered Wang Zai, military commissioner of Zhongwu, Li Yanzuo of Xuzhou, and others to serve as pacification commissioners on the southwest face of the Lu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong was furious. He ordered Wang Zai, military commissioner of Zhongwu, Li Yanzuo of Xuzhou, and others to serve as pacification commissioners on the southwest approach to Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遂復授沔太原節度，充潞府北面招討使。

translations.literal: Mian was then reappointed military commissioner of Taiyuan and made overall commander on the northern face of the Lu campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was then reappointed military commissioner of Taiyuan and made overall commander on the northern front of the Lu campaign.

sentences.zh: 沔與張仲武不協，方征兵幽州，乃移沔為鄭滑節度使，進位檢校司徒。

translations.literal: Mian did not get along with Zhang Zhongwu; as troops were being levied from Youzhou, Mian was transferred to military commissioner of Zheng-Hua and promoted to acting Grand Mentor of State.
translations.idiomatic: Mian and Zhang Zhongwu did not get along. While troops were being levied from Youzhou, Mian was transferred to military commissioner of Zheng-Hua and promoted to acting Grand Mentor of State.

sentences.zh: 既而以疾求歸洛陽，授太子太保，卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, citing illness, he requested to return to Luoyang; he was appointed Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, pleading illness, he asked to return to Luoyang. He was appointed Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince and died.

sentences.zh: 初，沔為忠武小校，從李光顏討淮西，為捉生將。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Mian was a junior officer in Zhongwu, he followed Li Guangyan in the campaign against Huai-West and served as a capture-and-reconnaissance officer.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Mian was a junior officer in Zhongwu, he followed Li Guangyan against Huai-West and served as a capture-and-reconnaissance officer.

sentences.zh: 前後遇賊血戰，鋒刃所傷，幾死者數四。

translations.literal: Before and after, he fought the enemy in bloody battles and was wounded by blades four times, nearly dying.
translations.idiomatic: Time and again he fought the enemy in bloody combat. Blades wounded him on four separate occasions, and he nearly died.

sentences.zh: 嘗傷重臥草中，月黑不知歸路，昏然而睡，夢人授之雙燭，曰：「子方大貴，此行無患，可持此而還。」

translations.literal: Once, badly wounded, he lay in the grass; the night was dark and he did not know the way back. He fell unconscious asleep, and dreamed someone gave him a pair of candles, saying: "You are about to attain great eminence. On this journey you need have no fear—you may take these and return."
translations.idiomatic: Once, gravely wounded, he lay in the grass. The night was black and he could not find the way back. He sank into sleep, and in a dream someone handed him a pair of candles, saying, "You are destined for great honor. On this march you need fear nothing—take these and go home."

sentences.zh: 既行，炯然有雙光在前。

translations.literal: As he went, two bright lights shone before him.
translations.idiomatic: As he walked, two bright lights burned ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 自後破虜危難，每行常有此光。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever he broke barbarians in peril, this light always went with him on the march.
translations.idiomatic: After that, whenever he broke the enemy in danger on campaign, those twin lights went before him.

sentences.zh: 及罷鎮後，雙光息。

translations.literal: After he left his command, the twin lights ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Once he left his command, the twin lights vanished.

sentences.zh: 五年，李德裕出鎮，罷沔為太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when Li Deyu left his post, Mian was dismissed as military commissioner and made Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when Li Deyu left office, Mian was removed from his command and made Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 明年，以太子太保致仕卒。

translations.literal: The next year he retired as Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince and died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he retired as Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince and died.

sentences.zh: 石雄，徐州牙校也。

translations.literal: Shi Xiong—Shi Xiong was a yamen guard officer of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiong was a guard officer in the Xuzhou military yamen.

sentences.zh: 王智興之討李同捷，以雄為石廂捉生兵馬使。

translations.literal: When Wang Zhixing campaigned against Li Tongjie, he made Xiong commander of the capture-and-reconnaissance troops of the Stone Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhixing marched against Li Tongjie, he made Xiong commander of the Stone Quarters' capture-and-reconnaissance troops.

sentences.zh: 勇敢善戰，氣淩三軍。

translations.literal: Brave and skilled in battle, his spirit overawed the whole army.
translations.idiomatic: Brave and skilled in battle, his fighting spirit overawed the entire army.

sentences.zh: 自智興以兵臨賊境，率先收棣州，雄先驅渡河，前無堅陣。

translations.literal: From the time Zhixing led troops to the rebel border, Xiong was first to capture Di Prefecture; as vanguard he crossed the river first and no enemy line could stand before him.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment Zhixing brought his army to the rebel frontier, Xiong was first to take Di Prefecture. As vanguard he crossed the river ahead of the rest, and no enemy line could hold against him.

sentences.zh: 徐人伏雄之撫待，惡智興之虐，欲逐之而立雄。

translations.literal: The men of Xuzhou admired Xiong's humane treatment of them and hated Zhixing's cruelty; they wished to drive Zhixing out and install Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: The men of Xuzhou admired how Xiong treated them and hated Zhixing's cruelty. They wanted to drive Zhixing out and put Xiong in his place.

sentences.zh: 智興以軍在賊境，懼其變生，因其立功，請授一郡刺史。

translations.literal: Zhixing, with his army still in enemy territory, feared a mutiny; taking advantage of Xiong's merit, he requested that Xiong be granted a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: With his army still in enemy country, Zhixing feared a mutiny. Citing Xiong's merit, he asked that Xiong be given a prefectural post.

sentences.zh: 朝廷征赴京師，授壁州刺史。

translations.literal: The court summoned him to the capital and appointed him prefect of Bi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court summoned him to the capital and appointed him prefect of Bi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 智興尋殺雄之素相善諸將士百余人，仍奏雄搖動軍情，請行誅戮。

translations.literal: Zhixing soon killed more than a hundred generals and soldiers who had been on good terms with Xiong, and still memorialized that Xiong had disturbed army morale and asked that he be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixing soon killed more than a hundred generals and soldiers who had been close to Xiong, and still memorialized that Xiong had unsettled the army and should be executed.

sentences.zh: 文宗雅知其能，惜之，乃長流白州。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong knew well his ability and valued him, and so instead had him exiled far to Bai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong knew his talent and valued him, and so instead had him exiled to distant Bai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太和中，河西党項擾亂，選求武士。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era the Tangut of Hexi were in turmoil, and the court sought warriors.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe reign the Tangut of Hexi were in turmoil, and the court searched for fighting men.

sentences.zh: 乃召還，隸振武劉沔軍為裨將，累立破羌之功。

translations.literal: Xiong was recalled and attached to Liu Mian's Zhenwu army as a subordinate general, winning repeated achievements in defeating the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was recalled and placed under Liu Mian in the Zhenwu army as a subordinate general, winning repeated victories over the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 文宗以智興故，未甚提擢，而李紳、李德裕以崔群舊將，素嘉之。

translations.literal: Because of Zhixing, Emperor Wenzong did not promote him greatly; but Li Shen and Li Deyu, as former generals of Cui Qun's command, had always admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Zhixing, Emperor Wenzong did not promote him far; but Li Shen and Li Deyu, who had once served under Cui Qun, had long admired him.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，回鶻寇天德，詔命劉沔為招撫回鶻使。

translations.literal: At the start of Huichang, when the Uyghurs raided Tiande, an edict appointed Liu Mian commissioner to pacify the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Huichang, when the Uyghurs raided Tiande, an edict appointed Liu Mian commissioner to pacify the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 三年，回鶻大掠雲、朔北邊，牙於五原。

translations.literal: In the third year the Uyghurs looted heavily along the Yun and Shuo northern frontier and made their camp at Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Uyghurs looted heavily along the Yun and Shuo northern frontier and pitched camp at Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 沔以太原之師屯於雲州。

translations.literal: Mian stationed the Taiyuan army at Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mian stationed the Taiyuan army at Yun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 沔謂雄曰：「黠虜離散，不足驅除。

translations.literal: Mian said to Xiong: "These cunning barbarians are scattered and not worth driving off outright.
translations.idiomatic: Mian said to Xiong, "These cunning barbarians are scattered—not worth chasing off in a full campaign.

sentences.zh: 國家以公主之故，不欲急攻。

translations.literal: Because of the princess the state does not wish to attack in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the princess, the court does not want a hurried attack.

sentences.zh: 今觀其所為，氣淩我輩。

translations.literal: Now judging by their conduct, their arrogance overmatches ours.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by what they are doing now, their arrogance outmatches ours.

sentences.zh: 若稟朝旨，或恐依違。

translations.literal: If we report to court for orders, I fear we shall meet with vacillation.
translations.idiomatic: If we ask the court for orders, I fear we will meet only hesitation.

sentences.zh: 我輩捍邊，但能除患，專之可也。

translations.literal: We who defend the frontier need only remove the harm—that may be done on our own authority.
translations.idiomatic: We who guard the frontier need only remove the threat. That we may do on our own authority.

sentences.zh: 公可選驍健，乘其不意，徑趨虜帳，彼以疾雷之勢，不暇枝梧，必棄公主亡竄。

translations.literal: You may choose elite fighters and, catching them unaware, strike straight at the barbarian camp; with the speed of sudden thunder they will have no time to brace themselves and are sure to abandon the princess and flee.
translations.idiomatic: Choose your best fighters, catch them off guard, and strike straight at the barbarian camp. Moving like sudden thunder, they will have no time to brace themselves and will surely abandon the princess and flee.

sentences.zh: 事茍不捷，吾自繼進，亦無患也。」

translations.literal: If the affair does not succeed, I shall follow up myself—there will be no danger even so."
translations.idiomatic: If the plan fails, I will follow up myself. Even then there will be no great risk."

sentences.zh: 雄受教，自選勁騎，得沙陁李國昌三部落，兼契苾拓拔雜虜三千騎，月暗夜發馬邑，徑趨烏介之牙。

translations.literal: Xiong accepted the instruction, personally selected crack cavalry, mustered three Shatuo tribes under Li Guochang plus Qibi and Tuoba and other mixed barbarians—three thousand horsemen in all—and on a dark night set out from Mayi, heading straight for Wujie's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong accepted the plan. He personally picked crack cavalry, mustered three Shatuo tribes under Li Guochang together with Qibi, Tuoba, and other allied barbarians—three thousand horsemen in all—and on a moonless night set out from Mayi straight for Wujie's camp.

sentences.zh: 時虜帳逼振武，雄既入城，登堞視其眾寡。

translations.literal: The barbarian camp then pressed close to Zhenwu; once Xiong entered the city he climbed the parapet to survey their numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian camp then pressed close to Zhenwu. Once inside the city, Xiong climbed the wall to gauge their strength.

sentences.zh: 見氈車數十，從者皆衣硃碧，類華人服飾。

translations.literal: He saw several dozen felt wagons; the attendants all wore vermilion and green, like Chinese dress.
translations.idiomatic: He saw several dozen felt wagons. The attendants all wore vermilion and green, in dress like that of Chinese.

sentences.zh: 雄令諜者訊之：「此何大人？」

translations.literal: Xiong ordered a scout to inquire: "What great personage is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiong sent a scout to ask, "What great personage is this?"

sentences.zh: 虜曰：「此公主帳也。」

translations.literal: The barbarian said: "This is the princess's camp."
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian answered, "This is the princess's camp."

sentences.zh: 雄喻其人曰：「國家兵馬欲取可汗。

translations.literal: Xiong instructed the man: "The state's army intends to take the khagan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong told the man, "The imperial army means to seize the khagan.

sentences.zh: 公主至此，家國也，須謀歸路。

translations.literal: The princess has come this far—this is her home and realm; you must plan a way back.
translations.idiomatic: The princess has come this far—this is her home and country. You must plan your return.

sentences.zh: 俟兵合時不得動帳幕。」

translations.literal: When the troops combine, do not move the tent curtains."
translations.idiomatic: When the armies join battle, do not stir the tent curtains."

sentences.zh: 雄乃大率城內牛馬雜畜及大鼓，夜穴城為十余門。

translations.literal: Xiong then assembled within the city all cattle, horses, and mixed livestock and large drums; by night they dug more than ten breaches in the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong then gathered inside the city all cattle, horses, and other livestock, together with great drums. By night they opened more than ten breaches in the wall.

sentences.zh: 遲明，城上立旗幟炬火，乃於諸門縱其牛畜，鼓噪從之，直犯烏介牙帳。

translations.literal: At daybreak they raised banners, torches, and signal fires on the wall, then at every breach drove out the livestock amid clamorous drumming and rushed after them, charging straight at Wujie's main camp.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they raised banners, torches, and signal fires on the wall, then at every breach drove out the livestock to the thunder of drums and charged after them straight at Wujie's main camp.

sentences.zh: 炬火燭天，鼓噪動地，可汗惶駭莫測，率騎而奔。

translations.literal: Torches lit the sky and the uproar shook the earth; the khagan was terrified beyond measure and fled on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Torches lit the sky and the uproar shook the earth. The khagan was terrified beyond reckoning and fled on horseback.

sentences.zh: 雄率勁騎追至殺胡山，急擊之。

translations.literal: Xiong led crack cavalry in pursuit to Mount Sha Hu, pressing the attack hotly.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong led crack cavalry in pursuit to Mount Sha Hu and pressed the attack hard.

sentences.zh: 斬首萬級，生擒五千，羊馬車帳皆委之而去。

translations.literal: They cut off ten thousand heads, took five thousand alive, and left behind sheep, horses, wagons, and tents in heaps.
translations.idiomatic: They took ten thousand heads, five thousand captives, and left sheep, horses, wagons, and tents abandoned in heaps.

sentences.zh: 遂迎公主還太原。

translations.literal: They then escorted the princess back to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: They then escorted the princess back to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 以功加檢校左散騎常侍、豐州刺名、兼御史大夫、天德防禦等使。

translations.literal: For his achievement he was further appointed acting Left Regular Grand Master of the Palace Retinue, prefect of Feng Prefecture, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and defense commissioner of Tiande.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was further appointed acting Left Regular Grand Master of the Palace Retinue, prefect of Feng Prefecture, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and defense commissioner of Tiande.

sentences.zh: 雄沈勇徇義，臨財甚廉。

translations.literal: Xiong was deep-spirited, courageous, and devoted to duty, and in matters of wealth very incorruptible.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was resolute, brave, and devoted to duty, and scrupulously honest where wealth was concerned.

sentences.zh: 每破賊立功，朝廷特有賜與，皆不入私室；

translations.literal: Whenever he won merit in defeating rebels the court specially rewarded him, yet he never kept the gifts for his private quarters;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he won merit against the rebels the court sent special rewards, yet he never kept them for his private quarters;

sentences.zh: 置於軍門，首取一分，余並分給，以此軍士感義，皆思奮發。

translations.literal: he placed them at the camp gate, took one share for himself first, and distributed the rest—all of which moved the soldiers with his righteousness and made them eager to fight.
translations.idiomatic: he placed them at the camp gate, took one share for himself, and divided the rest among the men. The soldiers were moved by his righteousness and burned to fight.

sentences.zh: 累遷檢校左僕射、河中尹、河中晉絳節度使。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to acting Left Vice Minister, magistrate of Hezhong, and military commissioner of the Hezhong-Jin-Jiang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to acting Left Vice Minister, magistrate of Hezhong, and military commissioner of the Hezhong-Jin-Jiang circuit.

sentences.zh: 俄而昭義劉從諫卒，其子稹擅主軍務，朝議問罪。

translations.literal: Before long Liu Congjian of Zhaoyi died; his son Zhen seized control of military affairs on his own, and court opinion called for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liu Congjian of Zhaoyi died. His son Zhen seized military affairs on his own authority, and court opinion demanded punishment.

sentences.zh: 令徐帥李彥佐為潞府西南面招撫使，以晉州刺史李丕為副。

translations.literal: Li Yanzuo, commander of Xu, was ordered pacification commissioner on the southwest face of Lu; Li Pi, prefect of Jin, was made his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanzuo, commander of Xu, was ordered to serve as pacification commissioner on the southwest approach to Lu; Li Pi, prefect of Jin, was made his deputy.

sentences.zh: 時王宰在萬善柵，劉沔在石會，相顧未進。
