translations.literal: At the time Wang Zai was at Wanshan Stockade and Liu Mian at Shihui; they looked at each other and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Zai held Wanshan Stockade and Liu Mian held Shihui. They faced each other and neither advanced.

sentences.zh: 雄受代之翌日，越烏嶺，破賊五砦，斬獲千計。

translations.literal: The day after Xiong received his replacement commission, he crossed Wuling, broke five rebel stockades, and took a thousand-odd heads and captives.
translations.idiomatic: The day after Xiong took up his new command, he crossed Wuling, broke five rebel stockades, and took more than a thousand heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 武宗聞捷大悅，謂侍臣曰：「今之義而有勇，罕有雄之比者。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong, hearing of the victory, was greatly pleased and said to his attendants: "Among men today who unite righteousness with courage, few compare with Xiong."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong heard of the victory he was greatly pleased and said to his attendants, "Among men today who join righteousness with courage, few can compare with Xiong."

sentences.zh: 雄既率先破賊，不旬日，王宰收天井關，何弘敬、王元逵亦收磁洺等郡。

translations.literal: Once Xiong had been first to break the rebels, within ten days Wang Zai recovered Tianjing Pass, and He Hongjing and Wang Yuankui also recovered Ci, Ming, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiong had broken the rebels first, within ten days Wang Zai recovered Tianjing Pass, and He Hongjing and Wang Yuankui recovered Ci, Ming, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 先是潞州狂人折腰於市，謂人曰：「雄七千人至矣。」

translations.literal: Earlier, a madman in Lu Prefecture had bowed at the waist in the market and told people: "Xiong and seven thousand men have arrived."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a madman in Lu Prefecture had bowed double in the market and told people, "Xiong and seven thousand men have arrived."

sentences.zh: 劉從諫捕而誅之。

translations.literal: Liu Congjian arrested and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congjian arrested and executed him.

sentences.zh: 及稹危蹙，大將郭誼密款請斬稹歸朝，軍中疑其詐。

translations.literal: When Zhen was hard pressed, the great general Guo Yi secretly pledged to behead Zhen and submit to the court; the army suspected it was a trick.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen was cornered, the great general Guo Yi secretly offered to behead Zhen and surrender to the court. The army suspected a ruse.

sentences.zh: 雄倡言曰：「賊稹之叛，郭誼為謀主。

translations.literal: Xiong declared publicly: "In Zhen the rebel's uprising, Guo Yi was the chief plotter.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong declared openly, "In Zhen's rebellion Guo Yi was the chief plotter.

sentences.zh: 今請斬稹，即誼自謀，又何疑焉？」

translations.literal: Now that he asks to behead Zhen, it is Yi's own scheme—why any doubt?"
translations.idiomatic: Now that he asks to behead Zhen, it is Yi's own design—why doubt him?"

sentences.zh: 武宗亦以狂人之言，詔雄以七千兵受降。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong also recalled the madman's words and ordered Xiong to accept the surrender with seven thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong also remembered the madman's words and ordered Xiong to accept the surrender with seven thousand men.

sentences.zh: 雄即徑馳潞州降誼，盡擒其黨與。

translations.literal: Xiong rode straight to Lu Prefecture to receive Yi's surrender and captured all his partisans.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong rode straight to Lu Prefecture to receive Yi's surrender and seized all his accomplices.

sentences.zh: 賊平，進加檢校司空。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified he was further promoted to acting Grand Master of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were pacified he was further promoted to acting Grand Master of Works.

sentences.zh: 王宰，智興之子，於雄不足，雄以轅門子弟善禮之。

translations.literal: Wang Zai was Zhixing's son and fell short of Xiong; Xiong treated him courteously as a commander's son.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zai was Zhixing's son and could not match Xiong, yet Xiong treated him courteously as a commander's son.

sentences.zh: 然討潞之役，雄有始卒之功，宰心惡之。

translations.literal: Yet in the Lu campaign Xiong had merit from first to last, and Zai inwardly resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the Lu campaign Xiong had merit from beginning to end, and Zai inwardly resented him.

sentences.zh: 及李德裕罷相，宰黨排擯雄，罷鎮。

translations.literal: When Li Deyu left the chancellorship, Zai's faction drove Xiong out and dismissed him from command.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Deyu left the chancellorship, Zai's faction forced Xiong out and stripped him of his command.

sentences.zh: 既而聞德裕貶，發疾而卒。

translations.literal: Soon after, hearing that Deyu had been demoted, he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, on hearing that Deyu had been demoted, he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：古所謂名將者，不必蒙輪拔距之材，拉虎批熊之力；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: What antiquity called a famous general need not possess the talent for vaulting wheels and pulling rafters, nor the strength to drag tigers and strike bears;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: What the ancients called a famous general did not have to possess the raw strength to vault over chariots or pull up house beams, nor the brute force to drag tigers and strike bears;

sentences.zh: 要當以義終始，好謀而成。

translations.literal: what matter is to keep faith from beginning to end and to succeed through careful planning.
translations.idiomatic: what mattered was to keep faith from first to last and to win through careful planning.

sentences.zh: 而阿跌昆仲，稟氣陰山，率多令範。

translations.literal: The Jie A Die brothers drew their spirit from the Yin Mountains and largely set a model of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The Jie A Die brothers drew their spirit from the Yin Mountains and, for the most part, set a standard of conduct.

sentences.zh: 讓家權於主婦，拒美妓於奸臣；

translations.literal: They yielded family authority to the mistress of the house and turned away beautiful entertainers offered by treacherous ministers;
translations.idiomatic: They yielded household authority to the mistress of the house and turned away the beautiful entertainers proffered by treacherous ministers;

sentences.zh: 章武恢復之功，義師之效也。

translations.literal: the restorative achievement of Emperor Xianzong was the effect of righteous armies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong's work of restoration was the fruit of righteous armies.

sentences.zh: 重胤忠於事上，仁於撫下，淮、蔡之役，勛亞光顏；

translations.literal: Wu Chongyin was loyal in serving his superiors and humane in caring for his subordinates; in the Huai-Cai campaign his merit was second only to Guangyan;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chongyin was loyal in serving his superiors and humane in caring for his men; in the Huai-Cai campaign his merit stood second only to Guangyan;

sentences.zh: 殿邦之臣也，不可多得。

translations.literal: a minister who steadies the realm—such men cannot easily be found.
translations.idiomatic: a minister who steadies the realm—men like that are not easily found.

sentences.zh: 王沛之擒僚婿，李祐之執賊渠，皆因事立功，轉禍為福。

translations.literal: Wang Pei's capture of the son-in-law and Li You's seizure of the rebel chieftain both won merit by seizing opportunities and turned misfortune into blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pei's capture of the son-in-law and Li You's seizure of the rebel chieftain both won merit by seizing opportunity and turned misfortune into blessing.

sentences.zh: 智則智矣，仁者不為！

translations.literal: Clever, yes—but a humane man would not do such things!
translations.idiomatic: Clever, yes—but a humane man would not have done such things!

sentences.zh: 而劉悟自恃太尤，世邀纘襲，至於赤族，報亦晚耶！

translations.literal: Liu Wu, trusting himself overmuch, for generations sought inherited succession—to the point of extermination of his clan; was the retribution not late indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wu, trusting himself too far, for generations sought hereditary succession—to the point where his clan was wiped out. Was the retribution not long in coming!

sentences.zh: 雄、沔負羽邊城，聲馳沙漠，奉迎貴主，摧破昆戎，不亦壯乎！

translations.literal: Xiong and Mian bore heavy responsibilities on the frontier, their fame racing across the desert; they escorted an imperial princess and crushed the Kun barbarians—was it not magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Xiong and Mian shouldered the frontier's heavy burden, their fame racing across the desert; they escorted an imperial princess and crushed the Kun barbarians—was that not magnificent!

sentences.zh: 雄能感於知己，不為無義，美哉！

translations.literal: That Xiong could be moved by one who knew his worth and would not act without righteousness—beautiful indeed!
translations.idiomatic: That Xiong could be moved by one who knew his worth and refused to act without righteousness—how fine!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：淮、鄆砥平，義將輸誠。

translations.literal: In praise: Huai and Yun were ground level; righteous generals offered their loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: When Huai and Yun were brought to heel, righteous generals offered their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 二兇受縛，亦其同惡。

translations.literal: The two villains were bound—yet their accomplices shared the guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Two villains were bound—yet their accomplices shared the guilt.

sentences.zh: 毀義棄忠，必殄爾宗。

translations.literal: Whoever destroys righteousness and abandons loyalty—your clan shall be wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever destroys righteousness and abandons loyalty—your clan shall be wiped out.

sentences.zh: 孰稱善將？

translations.literal: Who may be called good generals?
translations.idiomatic: Who may be called good generals?

sentences.zh: 劉沔、石雄。

translations.literal: Liu Mian and Shi Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian and Shi Xiong.
